My former colleague Leah Stodart explained all the tech around what makes the Shark mask so great (and why it's the best LED light mask our team has tried), but I'll give you the quick version:.

It features blue, red, and near-infrared light, meaning it can treat a variety of skincare concerns from acne to anti-aging.

It legitimately calms and clears my breakouts faster and more reliably (more so than the Solawave wand or Bye Acne device).

My skin gets smooth after using this mask consistently.

The built-in timer and remote make it easy to make using it more of a habit at the beginning or end of my day.

The cooling eye pads feel like heaven.

The hard shell mask fits my face better than other red light masks (though a flatter design is more ideal for travel).

Sources indicate that it's significantly more affordable than other major red light masks, even at full price. For $255, it's nearly unbeatable.

Though the Shark mask is an investment and not essential to a skincare routine, it makes a great gift to a loved one (that includes yourself!) and gives you the ability to have a skincare spa day at home, even if you only have eight minutes or so to spare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An key note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

If you find yourself stuck at any step of today's Hurdle, don't worry! We have you covered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today's NYT Strands hints will be easy if you love old television.

Strands, the New York Times' elevated word-search game, requires the player to perform a twist on the classic word search. Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. Every single letter in the grid will be part of an answer. There's always a theme linking every solution, along with the "spangram," a special, word or phrase that sums up that day's theme, and spans the entire grid horizontally or vertically.

By providing an opaque hint and not providing the word list, Strands creates a brain-teasing game that takes a little longer to play than its other games, like Wordle and Connections.

If you're feeling stuck or just don't have 10 or more minutes to figure out today's puzzle, we've got all the NYT Strands hints for today's puzzle you need to progress at your preferred pace.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The NYT Connections puzzle today is not too difficult if you love to gamble.

In a recent development, connections is the one of the most popular New York Times word games that's captured the public's attention. The game is all about finding the "common threads between words." And just like Wordle, Connections resets after midnight and each new set of words gets trickier and trickier—so we've served up some hints and tips to get you over the hurdle.

Sources indicate that if you just want to be told today's puzzle, you can jump to the end of this article for today's Connections solution. But if you'd rather solve it yourself, keep reading for some clues, tips, and strategies to assist you.

The NYT's latest daily word game has become a social media hit. The Times credits associate puzzle editor Wyna Liu with helping to create the upcoming word game and bringing it to the publications' Games section. Connections can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

It has been revealed that each puzzle features 16 words and each grouping of words is split into four categories. These sets could comprise of anything from book titles, software, country names, etc. Even though multiple words will seem like they fit together, there's only one correct answer.

It has been revealed that if a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake—players get up to four mistakes until the game ends.

Players can also rearrange and shuffle the board to make spotting connections easier. Additionally, each group is color-coded with yellow being the easiest, followed by green, blue, and purple. Like Wordle, you can share the results with your friends on social media.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Moon is looking noticeably less full now, although most of its surface is still illuminated. We're still in the Waning Gibbous phase, with the Moon getting a little smaller each night as we head towards the Third Quarter.

Industry observers note that as of Saturday, Nov. 28, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 81% of its surface visible.

According to recent reports, if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Oceanus Procellarum, as well as the Tycho Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Gassendi Crater, the Clavius Crater, and the Archimedes Crater. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11 and 15 landing spots, plus the Fra Mauro Highlands.

In North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24.

It takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA. Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a New Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around.

Fresh Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

It has been revealed that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Black Friday vs. Cyber Monday: Which day should you shop for the best deals?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that once two distinct deal-shopping days, Black Friday and Cyber Monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza.
  • While major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on major-ticket items (like TVs, Apple devices, smartwatches, headphones, and of course, Amazon's own devices).
  • If you're debating when you should start adding massive-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, you've come to the right place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that once two distinct deal-shopping days, Black Friday and Cyber Monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza. The lines really began to blur when the world shut down in 2020, and brick-and-mortar stores hosted online sales in lieu of in-person Black Friday events. In 2026, lines outside stores are practically nonexistent. We certainly can't see them.

While major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on major-ticket items (like TVs, Apple devices, smartwatches, headphones, and of course, Amazon's own devices). That includes discounts that beat Amazon's massively hyped October Prime Day deals.

If you're debating when you should start adding massive-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, you've come to the right place. After years of covering both sales extensively, here's our expert analysis.

Way back in the age of MySpace and AIM — aka 2005 — the National Retail Federation debuted the term "Cyber Monday" after realizing that the Monday after Thanksgiving saw a flood of online sales. This was likely due to shoppers using their faster internet connections at work on Monday morning to snag deals, or at least that's what they credited it to. That, of course, and the fact that online retailers wanted some of that holiday shopping bread, too. Thus, two distinct deal-shopping days were born: Black Friday, for those who wanted to shop in stores the day after Thanksgiving, and Cyber Monday, for those who preferred shopping from the comfort of their desks.

Over 20 years later, there's little — if any — real difference between the two due to the alleged "death of retail." Everyone and everything is online, so why wouldn't Black Friday be? Based on our years of experience covering both, we can truly say neither is a "better" day to shop. It really comes down to what you're looking for and how much demand there is for it. If you see a solid deal, grab it, no matter which sale title it falls under. There's not a tremendous amount of distinction anymore in terms of discounts on particular products, as there was in previous years. However, there are still rules to follow in some product categories: TV deals tend to be more dramatic and widespread for Black Friday, with a higher likelihood of selling out before the clock even turns to Cyber Monday, while waiting for Cyber Monday to double-check that there's not a upcoming, better laptop deal is often wise.

It has been revealed that but with the blurred lines of Cyber Week, many of these deals will cross over. As noted at BlackFriday.com, "Some TV deals will feature flashy discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but they might not have the specs you're after.".

In a recent development, TL;DR: The deals will be great for both shopping days, but it all depends on what you're looking for. If you see specs you like listed under a product at a price you like, grab it to be safe.

Black Friday proper falls on Nov. 27 in 2026, but it's honestly silly to even call it Black Friday at this point. It's no longer just on Friday — it's a month-long affair. You can shop deals at practically every retailer starting right after Halloween (before, even), with most labeling something an "early Black Friday deal" as early as November. Best Buy's official early Black Friday sale kicked off Nov. 6, while Target's began on Nov. 5. Amazon's actual Black Friday sale starts Nov. 19, but you can already find the "early Black Friday deal" tag on plenty of listings. In other words, if you want to get some early shopping done, have at it.

Once the clock strikes midnight on Friday, it's basically Cyber Monday (yes, even though it's actually Saturday). We don't make the rules. The deals won't change too much, but the search terms and official site banners will.

Recent findings suggest that officially, Cyber Monday is on Monday, Nov. 30 in 2026. Unofficially, it basically starts the second Black Friday ends, with retailers calling sales "Cyber Monday" deals as early as Saturday, Nov. 28. So basically, semantics — and it's easier to just think of the Cyber Week language as interchangeable.

Topics Black Friday Cyber Monday.

Black Friday will last most of November, but come Saturday, Nov. 28, it's Cyber Monday time. As we mentioned above, since Black Friday and Cyber Monday are basically one massive shopping holiday, you likely won't see that many changes in deals, just changes in the banners and advertising of them.

Industry observers note that cyber Monday sales will last from Saturday, Nov. 28 to midnight on Monday, Nov. 30. There's not a hard stop, as there's always deals that stay live for at least the day or two following, but the large bulk of the sale is over once Monday ends.

Industry observers note that as store policy, Target stores are closed on Thanksgiving Day, but are open for Black Friday beginning at 6 a.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27.

Walmart will be open from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27. Walmart has confirmed that physical stores will be closed on Thanksgiving Day "so associates can spend the day with their families.".

Industry observers note that all physical Best Buy locations will be closed on Thanksgiving. Doors will open at 6 a.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27 for shoppers and close at 10 p.m.

According to recent reports, all Kohl's stores are closed on Thanksgiving but are open for in-store shopping beginning at 5 a.m. local time on Nov. 27, per a press release.

If you are trying to get your hands on a PlayStation 5 right now, the real win is not a discount — it is simply finding one in stock at standard retail price. Between a global RAM shortage driven by the AI boom, which pushed Sony to hike console prices twice in under a year, and the massive hype around GTA 6, standalone console markdowns are nowhere to be found.

In a recent development, today, the PS5 Slim Digital Edition starts at $599.99, and the flagship PS5 Pro retails for $899.99. Depending on the model, that means PlayStation 5 hardware actually costs $150 to $200 more today than it did when the console originally launched in 2020.

In a recent development, for weeks, the hype around GTA 6 completely wiped out store shelves across the country — especially for the PS5 Pro. The good news is that major retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Amazon are finally restocking standard PS5 models at regular list price.

We recommend paying full sticker price, because third-party marketplace listings are barely worth looking at anyway — the few that are up are mostly refurbished units marked up to nearly double the retail cost, so we left them off our list.

Even at full sticker price, picking up a PS5 or PS5 Pro makes a lot of sense if you are upgrading for GTA 6 or catching up on Sony's massive library of current-gen games.

The standard PlayStation 5 Digital Edition gives you the core current-gen experience in a slim, compact design that fits easily into a media console. You get an 825GB ultra-high-speed SSD that cuts load screens to seconds, 4K TV output, up to 120 fps gameplay on supported titles, and Tempest 3D AudioTech.

Sources indicate that it also ships with Sony's DualSense wireless controller — featuring haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that add physical resistance when you pull a trigger or drive over rough terrain — and plays more than 8,500 backward-compatible PS4 games with smoother frame rates. Plus, if you ever decide you want to buy physical discs later, you can snap Sony's detachable disc drive right onto the side. Altra Running is best known for its wide toe box, which lets toes relax and helps prevent blisters, and for its zero-drop platform, meaning your heel and forefoot sit at the same height. While this design may not be the most fashionable, it has earned Altra a devoted following among runners and hikers who value comfort, stability, and a more natural stride.

Apparently, that rugged practicality extends to the apocalypse. In One Battle After Another, Leonardo DiCaprio’s character, Bob Furguson, wears a pair of all-weather Altra Lone Peaks. It feels like a convincing product placement for a shoe designed to survive whatever you throw at it. The Lone Peak is comfortable, durable, and capable on uneven terrain, making it a particularly good choice for runners who prefer trails over pavement. Altras aren’t at the top of our list of the best running shoes, but for hiking and trail running, they are strong contenders.

If you need a pair of shoes capable of surviving your own dystopian adventures, here are the best Altra promo codes and Altra coupon codes at the moment available.

It has been revealed that the Lone Peaks are iconic and easily recognizable. However, if you prefer a different model than Bob Ferguson's, the hiking version of the Lone Peaks is available with a $36 discount. Currently, there are many styles of men’s shoes on sale, with discounts reaching up to 50% on select styles.

Maybe you’re considering Altra running shoes because a more widely known brand, like Brooks or Nike, has a toe box that’s too small. In that case, Altra doesn’t make only trail running shoes. The Fwd Via is Altra’s version of the Brooks Glycerin—the ultra-cushioned road running shoe. It’s also on sale, along with various running shoes, at 20% off.

You can get free standard delivery in 5-7 business days (no weekend delivery) when you order through Altra! If you need your shoes in a rush, there’s 2-day shipping (no weekend delivery) for $16.95, and next-day delivery (Saturday and Sunday orders ship on Mondays) for $22.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Motley Fool is the O.G. stock and investment advice website, dating back to the early days of the Internet, when WIRED’s website was still called hotwired.com. It started as a tip sheet in the early ‘90s by brothers Tom and David Gardner, and it rode a wave of hype to become a cult phenomenon, viewed with equal interest and skepticism by the established investment class. Thirty years and a whole bunch of books later, The Motley Fool now feels like the established investment class, with a Stock Advisor subscription service offering stock tips that were shown in a 2017 study led by Penn State to consistently beat the S&P 500.

The Motley Fool is not a single service. Rather, it’s a suite of stock-tips and analysis services, packaged in different bundles. The three main tiers are Stock Advisor ($199), Epic ($499), and Epic Plus ($1,999). Each higher tier offers more stock tips per month, more comprehensive data and research on potential investments, and more sophisticated analysis tools. The Epic Plus tier also offers access to “moneymaker” investment portfolios that are touted to follow Warren Buffett’s investment strategy. Generally, the site advises beginning investors with smaller portfolios to stick to the basic Stock Advisor tips to start out. The Fool also tends to recommend buying at least 50 stocks and holding them for at least 5 years, so it’s not a day-trading tool. Anyway, it’s often hard to find the right links to receive Motley Fool membership discounts. Go to this Motley Fool subscription discount page here for as much as half off the Stock Advisor, Epic, and Epic Plus Bundles for the first year only.

The website tends to offer a wide range of Motley Fool subscription discounts, depending on what URL you reach. Honestly, it’s a little confusing (and maybe infuriating, if you accidentally paid too much.) Motley Fool’s most popular option, Stock Advisor, offers the fabled market-beating “Top 10 Stocks to Buy Now,” plus portfolio analysis, analyst news, and monthly stock rankings. The best Motley Fool Stock Advisor discount I’ve seen at the moment comes by locking in your subscription for two years at $149 (as opposed to the nominal price of $199 per year.) Note that if you lock in a one-year subscription, Stock Advisor is yours for $99 a year, or $100 off.

If you want to begin investing but aren’t sure where to start, I’d recommend reading Motley Fool’s “Best Stocks to Buy Now: Our Buy-and-Hold Picks,” which is updated monthly. With thousands of publicly traded companies to choose from, many investors don't know where to start. That, along with this year’s stock market volatility due to the Iran conflict, tariff uncertainty, and fears of a weakening economy, makes things even shakier. But with this updated article, folks can gain insider knowledge to make the best financial decisions for their specific needs.

For better or worse, I’ve become a podcast person. Like so many people, I find them a great way to passively learn while doing other tasks. Motley Fool offers a variety of podcasts to help you achieve your goals or find financial stability. There’s the Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing podcast, which releases new episodes daily at 4pm (Eastern time). This podcast is for stock investors, offering a “long-term perspective on business news with The Motley Fool's investment analysts,” and weekend episodes feature a mix of personal finance advice and longer-form interviews. There’s also the Rule Breaker Investing podcast, which airs on Wednesdays and features David Gardner, co-founder of The Motley Fool. During the show, Gardner shares his insights into “today's most innovative and disruptive publicly traded companies” and offers advice on how everyday people can profit from them using unorthodox methods.

It can be difficult (and scary, TBH) to determine which retirement strategy is right for you and your financial situation. Your retirement plan determines how much you contribute annually, how it's taxed, how withdrawals work, what you can invest in, and how much you pay in fees. Motley Fool offers a wide range of content to help you decide which retirement plans work best for your financial situation, including: 401(k) plans, IRA, Roth IRA, Nondeductible IRA, Keogh plan, and more. With this valuable tool, Motley Fool lays out all the information you’ll need, including employer-sponsored plans, individual retirement accounts, and plans for self-employed individuals and small business owners.

It has been revealed that most Motley Fool intends offer a 30-day money-back guarantee on the membership fee. This is not enough time to decide whether the stock tips have panned out, of course—but it is enough time to determine whether you think you’ll find the service useful and whether you’ll actually use it. This guarantee applies to most Motley Fool promotional offers, including the Motley Fool stock advisor promo code 2026 deals.

Speaking of gaming, we named the Govee AI Gaming Sync Box Kit the best lights for gaming, which reviewer Simon Hill praised as “easily one of the best smart lighting options for gamers.” He rated it as an 8/10. WIRED recommends it for its vibrant colors, accurate screen syncing, versatility, ability to customize, and, as a plus, it works with Google Home or Amazon Alexa.

The Govee Envisual T2 is the best light for your TV, as it syncs lights to what’s happening on your TV to turn your living room into your own personal IMAX-esque experience. Prefer being outside? We named the Govee Permanent Outdoor Lights Pro as our favorite outdoor light, even putting it in our Best Christmas Lights guide. We liked the ability to customize the lights via the app, which has a wide choice of animated scenes covering different holidays, tons of colorful styles, or you can opt for a classic white light for a classy look.

According to recent reports, with Walmart’s Black Friday deals, you can get up to 50% off everything, including tech, toys, home goods, fashion, auto, sports, outdoor gear, holiday essentials, seasonal decor, and more. Walmart has thousands of flash deals that change weekly, with up to 65% off tech, appliances, end-of-season, and holiday items. Be sure to check often to find the best rotating deals. It offers free grocery delivery, free shipping with no order minimum, fuel savings, and early access to promotions and events. Plus, you can try Walmart+ free for 30 days to see if the service is right for you or your family. The annual plan is $98 (roughly $8 per month) after the trial, meaning you’ll get $57 in savings annually.

This card not only helps you build credit but also doesn’t require an annual fee. When you apply for a OnePay Card, you’ll first be considered for the OnePay CashRewards Mastercard. If you don’t qualify, you’ll be considered for a OnePay Walmart Spend Card. Interested applicants can apply online at Walmart.com, in the Walmart app, or in-store.

Being a Walmart+ member comes with many perks, including 5% cash back when you shop at Walmart with Plus and 1.5% cash back on all other purchases, with zero annual fees. According to recent reports, black Friday deals are coming in hot and heavy. We're inundated with fresh price drops on laptops, headphones, fitness trackers, and everything in between. And yes, we're seeing a huge number of price drops on Apple.

Wading through the deals on iPads, MacBooks, and AirPods, it's tough to ignore T-Mobile's massive sale on iPhones. If you've been waiting until now to upgrade, you're in luck: For limited-time, the Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free at T-Mobile. Yes, you read that right.

Industry observers note that T-Mobile keeps things surprisingly flexible when it comes to qualifying for this Black Friday deal. You can port your existing phone number from an eligible rival carrier to a qualifying T-Mix proposal, and T-Mobile covers the full cost of the phone. Alternatively, existing customers can trade in an eligible phone in any condition on a qualifying T-Mix plan.

T-Mobile distributes the full discount as 36 monthly bill credits. If you leave T-Mobile or cancel your line before that three-year payment plan ends, the credits stop immediately, and you will owe the remaining balance on the device.

You are also still required to pay local sales tax on the phone's full $1,199 retail value upfront, plus T-Mobile's standard $35 device connection fee per line at checkout. Unfortunately, you can't escape those upfront charges.

Score the Apple iPhone 18 Pro for free with T-Mobile over Black Friday.

Topics Black Friday Gaming Pokemon Trading Cards.

If you spot a solid discount on a Pokémon TCG pack, box, or collection you haven’t seen before (like a 30th Celebration ETB, Delta Reign Booster Bundle, etc.), it’s worth buying now rather than waiting for Black Friday.

When you see a particular price drop, that deal is more likely specific to one or several sellers than to the industry market price across all sellers — depending on their own stock allocations. When that stock is gone, it’s uncertain whether those sellers will have any more units coming in, or even at the same lower price point.

Although more Pokémon cards are being printed than ever in 2026, the Pokémon TCG still has the same glitch that sees any readily available selection of packs, or boxes of packs, being sold for above MSRP: There is nowhere near enough supply to meet the demand.

As a result, prices for readily available cards are dictated by market price: estimated by factors like pull rates, the most valuable cards in an expansion, how many print runs an expansion has had, and their overall contribution to the meta.

Day-to-day deals vary between standard Pokémon TCG retailers like Amazon, Walmart, and Target — but the best Black Friday deals are likely to be from third-party sellers operating through those storefronts. There are a lot of sellers competing for sales with one another to offload their stock, and Black Friday is still the ideal season to undercut other Pokémon TCG merchants. Keep checking this guide and store listings each day for the best newly revealed deals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving has come and gone, but one holiday tradition is still to come thanks to a weather delay.

The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is an annual touchstone for lots of folks, and it's almost here. As always, there are lots of things to know about it, such as when it starts, where you can watch it, and, this year especially, whether the weather will affect the parade as expected. Let's get into it.

First and foremost, the parade starts at 8:30 a.m. ET and runs until noon on Saturday. Yes, you read that right: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is not actually on Thanksgiving Day this year. There are very good reasons for that, which we'll get to in a second.

Industry observers note that it's worth noting that, unlike most other live televised events, it will not air simultaneously in every time zone. Instead, per NBC News, it will air from 8:30 to around noon in each time zone, so no matter where you are, turn the TV on at 8:30.

The parade will air on NBC, so if you have a TV that gets local channels via cable, an antenna, or another way to watch TV, just turn on NBC.

If you don't have any of those things, Peacock will work, too. I should note that you'll need at least Peacock Premium to stream your local NBC station, and there is no free trial for that. You'll either have to pay $12.99 per month or borrow someone else's login. According to NBC News, this year's parade will feature 100 inflatables in total, the most they've ever used for one of these. You can see the full balloon lineup on the Macy's website, but rest assured that all your favorites are likely included, like Sonic the Hedgehog and the Pink Panther. There are also new ones, like a DoorDash float and a GEICO float. One float will also act as a tribute of sorts for Fiona the hippo, which is nice.

According to recent reports, performers include Teddy Swims and Megan Moroney on the main stage, with other floats featuring acts such as the Baha Men, Blues Traveler, Icona Pop, and Devo. There's a little something for everyone.

And now for the bad news: There's a weather system moving up the East Coast that has caused the parade organizers to reschedule it this year, per NBC News.

In a recent development, two storms combined into one in the American South, with the result expected to bring wind gusts of up to 45mph to New York City starting on Thursday morning. This is a problem because the city has an upper limit of 34mph for gusts regarding big inflatable objects. The parade was still scheduled for Thursday until the middle of Wednesday afternoon, when organizers and New York City officials decided to push it back to Saturday.

Unfortunately, that means you'll need a plan B for Thursday morning entertainment, but, more importantly, this should keep everyone who planned to attend the parade on Thursday safe.

WIRED reviewers have tried and liked a couple of machines from Diletta, a line of Italian-made, classic semiautomatics exclusive to Seattle Coffee Gear, and they’re all on sale today through December 14.

Sources indicate that when our reviewer tested the Bello+ in 2024, she appreciated the stylish, industrial design (handmade in Milan) and easily maneuverable steam wand. Best Traditional Espresso Machine in our guide to the best, the Mio is stylish and built to last, with an analog design and a two-year warranty. It also makes for a solid first “real” espresso machine with its built-in shot timer and pressure gauge.

Fellow set some pretty lofty expectations with the release of its sleek Aiden coffee maker in 2024, and according to former WIRED reviewer and espresso expert Matthew Korfhage, the brand didn't disappoint on its first attempt at an espresso machine. The ability to adjust flow rates and pressure curves was once the province of, as Korfhage put it, only the “richest and nerdiest of nerds.” But Fellow now allows you—yes, you, at home in your kitchen—to fine-tune how water moves through the grounds, unlocking previously unforeseen dimensions of flavor.

When we tested this machine, we liked it for a variety of reasons, including an easy-to-use milk frother and two swappable bean hoppers, which are especially helpful if you like to switch to decaf in the afternoons. It comes in a variety of finishes, but note that Beige is the cheapest of all right now, at only $915.

This flashy, design-oriented semiautomatic (“a steampunk gasworks of a thing,” according to Korfhage) is quite dramatic in person. It has a dual boiler—meaning you can froth milk at the same time you’re pulling a shot—and it comes with a nice set of accessories, including a tamper and milk pitcher. Note that this sale is on the second-gen machine, which features expanded grinder settings and a new portafilter.

The Best Semiautomatic Machine for Most People, the Barista Express is a longtime Reviews team favorite and platonic ideal of an espresso machine, with its pressure gauge and industrial-looking steam wand. If you want a built-in grinder without dropping four figures, this is your machine and your sale.

Formerly the Linea Classic, De’Longhi’s Classic is the best bare-bones espresso machine we’ve tried, with a pressure gauge, 15-bar pump, and updated thermoblock system. I used one for a full year and, while it’s not as foolproof as a semiautomatic, it was easy enough for morning espresso shots and cappuccinos; I even pulled off some rudimentary latte art with its steam wand.

According to recent reports, the Vertuo Pop+ is our favorite pod maker for espresso. The Deluxe model adds a larger, side-mount water tank (37 ounces to the original’s 25 ounces) and new finishes, including this white one, a matte black-and-gold, and a sort of gunmetal gray.

It has been revealed that OK, yes, this is not an espresso machine, but it is Korfhage's personal favorite coffee maker. “No device I know makes single-mug drip coffee this delicious with such ease and simplicity,” he writes in his review of the machine. It's perfect for just one or two people who don't need an entire carafe's worth of joe in the morning but also enjoy pour-over-style coffee and have no desire to futz with a Chemex.

According to recent reports, when we reviewed this semiautomatic in 2024, we appreciated its slim profile, consistent shots, and built-in burr grinder. The cold-brew setting is more of a gimmick than a way to make actual cold brew, and some design choices are a bit quirky. Even so, it’s a beautiful, industrial-looking machine that takes up only 12 inches of counter space.

Ninja sometimes has a reputation for doing too much, but this semiautomatic is a solid beginner-friendly option that pulls good shots. It’s got a built-in grinder and milk frother, the latter of which can make cold foam and even has a setting for plant-based milk. In true Ninja fashion, the machine also has settings for drip coffee and cold brew, but neither impressed our tester, so I wouldn’t buy it for those features alone.

Recent findings suggest that in May of this year, WIRED’s UK team did a blind taste test of espresso made with a variety of machines, including the Terra Kaffe TK-02 (below) and this Philips Café Aromis 8000 Series. The Philips won overall for its flavorful, balanced espresso and lattes. Our US Reviews team will be testing the Philips soon for our own guide, but you can see what the fuss is all about ahead of that with this 20-percent-off deal.

Recent findings suggest that our favorite pod machine for cold brew also has an Espresso setting that dispenses 2-ounce shots of espresso-style concentrate—perfectly chilled for iced coffee drinks. This is a huge machine and a huge investment (it only takes proprietary pods that cost more than $2 apiece), but if you have much love for cold coffee drinks (or espresso martinis) and little time to mess with a toddy or other manual machine, it will get you top-tier results within minutes.

Whether you want consistent espresso on the go or just prefer doing things the hard way, the Flair is our favorite manual espresso machine. It's how it was done in the old days, when pulling a shot was physically pulling a shot. It's not often on sale, so if you'd been considering it for a gift or for yourself this is a rare opportunity to save 20 percent.

Amazon (with attached milk carafe).

According to recent reports, look, not everyone has the time or patience for the romance and ritual of espresso making, and that's OK. A weekday morning is not often the time for fitzing and futzing, and sometimes any task beyond pushing a button is enough to push you into the Starbucks drive-thru. This Bosch model has a touchscreen with many drink options downloaded via firmware, and former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage appreciated that it lets you steam milk inside the machine or in a separate container, if your family uses multiple types of milk.

According to recent reports, korfhage tested Terra Kaffe's newer Demi and said it was perhaps the “dead-simplest fully automatic espresso machine I've yet encountered that still makes good coffee,” with just a dial and a button. Right now it's $200 off, or $300 off with a coffee subscription (Terra-Kaffe offers a house blend specifically made for its own machines). Its bigger sibling, the TK-02, impressed our tester with its convenience, ease of use, front-facing water filter, and milk carafe. Though it didn't come out on top during an espresso blind taste test we conducted earlier this year, it's still a great-looking machine that's easy to use. It's also a whopping $400 off (or $500 with a coffee subscription) for Black Friday.

Atlas (3-month Gift subscription).

Atlas (6-month Gift subscription).

According to recent reports, maybe you or your recipient already has an espresso machine; in that case, they’ll need some quality beans. Our favorite coffee subscription, Atlas Coffee Club, has a newly introduced gift option on offer for Black Friday: a quarterly subscription of three bags of unique, globally sourced coffee every three months for $59. You can choose any roast you want, including espresso roast and even Nespresso pods. If you’d rather buy an ongoing subscription for yourself, your first bag is free with Atlas’ Black Friday sale.

Former barista and WIRED contributing reviewer Pete Cottell likes this little scale that includes three magnetic add-ons: a platform, a metal dosing cup, and a catch cup that fits directly onto almost any portafilter.

If grounds are sticking to the plastic components of your coffee grinder, Cottell recommends adding this durable, stylish spray bottle to your espresso setup.

Cottell likes situating this mat underneath your espresso setup, as the lip contains spills, and the textured portion is great for drying tools post-washing.

Sources indicate that some machines come with a tamper; others don't. If yours doesn’t, Cottell recommends you get this one. The spring-loaded base unloads 15 pounds of force to create a perfectly flat puck inside your portafilter. (A click lets you know when to stop pushing, so it’s great for beginners too.).

In a recent development, we're closely monitoring inventory at all the major retailers and are cautiously optimistic it will be restocked for the holiday shopping season. On the question of if/when the limited-edition Zelda Switch 2 will be restocked, a Nintendo spokesperson provided this not-entirely-reassuring statement to Mashable: "Although we cannot provide detailed information, we are striving to ensure that we can supply our products to those who want them.".

Between automated bot armies scooping digital drops, surprise order cancellations at Walmart, and inventory vanishing in seconds on Amazon, this custom black-and-gold console feels like a myth. But while digital storefronts look completely barren, stock is actively circulating behind the scenes.

Before getting into the restock details, bookmark these retailer pages to check for surprise drops:.

Nintendo Store — Out of stock right now, but you can add it to your wishlist to get pinged the second a restock hits.

Amazon — Dropping tiny batches of consoles randomly throughout the day.

Walmart — Stock exists but only for third-party listings selling at way over market price, so make sure your in-stock email alerts are turned on.

Target — Sold out online, but periodic drops have taken place in-store.

Best Buy — Sold out online, but select stores ran midnight openings on Nov. 5 with walk-in stock.

GameStop — Online orders are off; you will have to walk into a store to find one.

It has been revealed that the feeding frenzy is being supercharged by Nintendo’s staggered release calendar. While the custom Zelda 40th Anniversary hardware dropped first on Oct. 29, the flagship game driving demand — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 — arrived on Thursday, Nov. 5.

The remake rebuilds the 1998 classic from the ground up with modernized controls, a fully orchestrated soundtrack, reworked dungeon puzzles, and expanded Hyrule environments. Since the $520 console doesn’t include the game, everyone is rushing to lock down a system before launch day.

The package includes the special-edition Switch 2 system sporting a custom black-and-gold finish, themed Joy-Con 2 controllers, and a matching dock decorated with the gold Triforce emblem. It retains the platform's signature flexibility, letting you switch between TV, Tabletop, and Handheld modes whenever you want. In a recent development, watch for Walmart+ early-access paywalls — Walmart frequently locks headline console drops behind paid Walmart+ subscriptions for the first 30 to 60 minutes. If you have a membership, keep that tab signed in; if not, wait for the general public window to unlock.

Thanks to hookup apps like Tinder and Pure, we can get “dates” (and I use that term loosely) with the tap of a button. Finding a sexy new friend can be as straightforward as ordering a pizza. As for the quality? That’s about the same as your pizza — hit or miss, depending on the time of day, where you’re located, and how hungry you are.

My goal is simple: to find the best apps for every kind of dater, including the one-night-stand crowd. I also consulted sex and relationship experts about being upfront, setting boundaries, and taking things offline.

Industry observers note that tinder is my top pick for most people looking for a hookup. If you’d rather keep your real name off your profile and be direct about your turn-ons, try Pure. Feeld is where I’d start for kink, non-monogamy, and exploring your sexuality. For queer men, I’d start with Grindr, or Sniffies if you’re specifically interested in cruising. HER is my pick for queer women. Hinge is worth considering for an ongoing casual connection, but be upfront: Plenty of people there want a relationship. AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections.

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups.

Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups.

Pure — best for anonymous hookups.

OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

Sources indicate that you don’t have to pretend you’re looking for a relationship to get a date. If you want a one-night stand or a regular FWB, say so.

Sources indicate that "Hookup apps help prevent situations where people are on mainstream dating sites with the intention of having a casual hookup but are unclear about these intentions," Suzannah Weiss, sex/couples therapist and resident sexologist for Erojoy, tells Mashable. "They also give women a space to be openly sexual creatures without judgment.".

Once you've matched, reach out, be honest, and follow through! "Strategy dates within the first conversation or else you'll get tired out from having a bunch of conversations that aren't going anywhere," Weiss indicates.

It has been revealed that as you may know, I've tested a lot of dating apps (like, a lot). But if someone asks me for the quickest way to find a hookup, I still tell them Tinder. CEO Spencer Rascoff is trying to move the app away from its "hookup reputation" to attract Gen Z and bring in more women, but that's probably not why you're here.

Industry observers note that either way, people are coming back. Tinder's daily active users grew year over year in September for the first time in three and a half years, per Match Group's third-quarter results. Tinder also notes it's made over 100 billion connections worldwide since launch.

It's built for quick connections, not long love stories (though some people, including Mashable's Tech Editor, met their long-term partner on the app).

Read our full review of Tinder.

"Tinder, hands down, is the best app for hookups," Michelle Herzog, LMFT and AASECT-certified sex therapist, tells Mashable. "Over the past decade or so, it's morphed from being the early 20s hookup central to a place for adults of all ages to go for a quick one-nighter." Weiss adds that it's "probably the most popular hookup app among college students.".

Tinder has added a lot of features that feel more relationship-y lately, like turning "Double Date" into "Modes" and launching its own reality show, Double Date Island. I still think it's the best app for casual flings. Its 2026 trend predictions even included "Clear-Coding," aka being upfront about what you want so nobody wastes their time. (Which, honestly, is my No. 1 rule for hookup apps.).

According to recent reports, if you'd feel better with your friends there, try Group Hangouts. It introduced in the U.S. on Sept. 30 and started rolling out in the U.K. on Nov. 23. You and at least two friends pick an activity and "like" other groups. If at least one person from each group likes the other, everyone ends up in a group chat to make plans. Double Date works the same way, just with you and one friend.

Sources indicate that there's also the "Events" tab, where you can RSVP to low-key hangouts like bar trivia or Chinatown mahjong. It expanded to London, Manchester, and Birmingham in November, and about 30 percent of events are free. Tinder is also testing an AI-powered "Missed Connections" feature in Canada and Australia that indicates you a weekly list of people you've physically crossed paths with. I'm super curious whether that one makes it to the U.S.

Sources indicate that of course, there's AI, too, including a "Chemistry" matchmaker and an algorithm that prioritizes "Sparks" (real back-and-forth conversations). I'd still take the algorithm's suggestions with a grain of salt. "Algorithmic curation, at its current level of sophistication, is very good at showing you more of what you've already responded to and significantly less good at showing you what could work better," claims Caroline Millet, a dating burnout coach and former matchmaker. "If your 'type' is so good, why are you still looking?" One thing AI can't do is talk for you: Rascoff says AI agents are banned on Tinder and Hinge.

On the safety side, Tinder now requires fresh members to scan their face (Face Check) before they can join. It started in California in October 2025 and has expanded since. It's not perfect. Scammers have found workarounds, and an October Senate report found that, as of late 2025, Tinder hadn't updated most of its AI scam detection models in years. (Match added a new one this year.) Match Group says Face Check and its other safety updates have cut exposure to potential bad actors by more than 60 percent, and it invests $125 million a year in trust and safety. My advice? If your match gets weird about their photos or wants to move to WhatsApp right away, unmatch.

Read our full review of AdultFriendFinder.

Sources indicate that pure is for the adventurous dater (with a growing Gen Z and millennial fan club) who is so over the mainstream options and the endless stream of low-effort "heys." If you want an uncomplicated, no-strings-attached hookup where you can be direct about your desires without judgment, this is the app. It's unconventional, artsy, and built for anonymity. In my experience, it's also the exact place to be for steamy conversations or super-hot phone sex with a stranger. Plus, Pure says its people are split 60/40 between men and women — a surprisingly balanced ratio.

I picked Pure because it's "hot, weird, and way better than Bumble" for making casual connections. Its best features are designed for direct, exciting encounters: chats disappear after 24 hours unless you both agree to keep them, and you don't have to put your real name on your profile.

In my four weeks of testing this anonymous hookup app, I was honestly surprised by the results. The conversations were leagues above what I've found on other apps, and I received hundreds of likes daily, even outside of a major city like Newly introduced York. While anonymity can be a concern, Pure balances it with safety features like Photo Verification and a "True Photo" request, which lets you ask for a live photo in your chat to confirm you're talking to a real person.

To combat the "app fatigue," Pure rolled out a major feed redesign in April. You'll now see one profile at a time, making the experience feel much more intentional. The organization also added newly introduced "Profile Aesthetics" so you can customize your ad with loud color patterns (like bright pink or periwinkle). Bonus: Your "Turn-ons" are now front and center, and a new "Mutual Turn-Ons" view instantly highlights the kinks and interests you share with a potential match before you even say hello.

Sources indicate that pure is also getting serious about safety. In December 2025, the app launched "Safety Signal," a feature that lets you share your location and date details with a trusted contact when you take things offline. In August 2026, Pure added "My Media Rules," a digital bouncer that lets you set universal boundaries to auto-block all incoming nudes, turn off media sharing, or adjust photo permissions on a chat-by-chat basis. In the UK, Pure also requires age verification before owners can post their first ad.

Recent findings suggest that "Consent should not begin when two people meet in person. It begins with how someone communicates, what they send and whether they respect a boundary the first time," says Sandra Hatton, a professional matchmaker and founder of When We First. "Technology can create another layer of protection, but it should support consent, not replace the responsibility of users to behave respectfully.".

That said, it's a space to navigate with intention. Anonymity is the whole point of Pure, but it shouldn't mean flying blind. "Anonymous should never mean untraceable to YOU," says Erica Arrechea, founder and CEO of Cinqe Matchmaking. "Before meeting someone, know who you're actually meeting. Meet publicly first!".

It has been revealed that pure doesn't have built-in background checks, so I'd look for the Photo Verification badge and send a True Photo request before you meet. (Here's how to vet your Pure matches.).

Weiss also notes that Pure isn't as specifically geared toward the kink and queer communities as Feeld, so you may encounter more straight cis men who are just looking for a conquest. The biggest trade-off is its smaller user base compared to mainstream apps like Tinder, though its recent 95 percent year-over-year registration growth and new status as a top-8 grossing lifestyle app in the U.S., UK, and France show it's rapidly closing the gap.

I know, I know: Hinge is supposedly "designed to be deleted." But honestly, I think it's one of the best apps for finding a regular hookup, especially if you like a little connection first. If you live in a reasonably populated area and Tinder gives you the ick, Hinge is a really good alternative.

According to recent reports, just know that plenty of people on Hinge want a relationship, so please be upfront about wanting something casual. I like it best for finding a regular FWB. If you want someone to come over tonight, I'd try a different app.

Industry observers note that hinge's "Dating Intentions" section lets you say exactly what you're looking for, and according to the app, 75 percent of Gen Z daters check it before sending a "like." So if you want something short-term, say so. It saves everyone time.

It has been revealed that and don't stress too much about your opener. In Hinge's October flirting report, 65 percent of Gen Z daters stated they'd rather someone flirt a little awkwardly but make their interest obvious than be smooth and leave them guessing. (Same, honestly.).

I also love that Hinge lets free people see everyone who "likes" them (one at a time). Most apps blur those photos until you pay. (Looking at you, eharmony.) You get eight free "likes" a day and can chat with matches for free. Hinge also picks out "Standouts" (profiles the algorithm thinks are your best potential matches), but you need a "Rose" to like them, and you only get one free Rose a week.

If you want more filters but don't want to pay for Hinge+ or HingeX, there might be another option soon. Hinge is testing a cheaper subscription tier with extra filters and custom location boundaries, and it's supposed to launch by the end of 2026.

When you're ready to meet up, "Date Ideas" lets you add three date options to your profile, like grabbing drinks or seeing live music. Matches can pick an idea and a time before they send a "like," so you can skip the "we should hang out sometime" back-and-forth.

Recent findings suggest that in June, Hinge also launched its "Signals" badge. The purple heart shows up on verified users who've recently been "Thoughtful Participants," like messaging their matches and confirming dates. It's helpful, but it doesn't guarantee someone won't flake. "Treat app features as additional information, not proof of intention," claims Hatton. "A badge or longer response window can be helpful, but seriousness ultimately shows up through behavior.".

If you get stuck on what to say, Hinge's AI-powered "Convo Starters" feature suggests icebreakers based on someone's profile. I'd keep AI away from your photos, though. Hinge states 88 percent of its daters are uncomfortable with AI-generated profile pictures.

According to recent reports, hinge also now requires upcoming owners to complete "Face Check," a video-selfie scan, in a growing number of regions. Hinge indicates the scan doesn't guarantee someone's identity or safety, though. On Oct. 1, it also announced a new approach to minor harassment: Human moderators can matter a warning and require an educational walkthrough before someone can use the app again.

If you're a woman or non-binary person who wants something casual without a flood of creepy messages, Bumble is where I'd start. Yes, it ended its famous "women message first" rule in August. But it's still way more structured than Tinder: Anyone can send one opening message, and the chat stays locked until the other person replies.

"Bumble is a helpful app for women who want to avoid being creeped on and only hear from men they're interested in," Weiss tells Mashable. And if you want someone who's upfront about wanting "fun, casual dates" or "intimacy, without commitment," you can find them here, too.
