Whoever gets that opening message now has 72 hours to reply, up from 24, which takes a lot of pressure off. The change came straight from owners, too. In a Bumble survey, 66 percent of women mentioned they actually prefer men to send the first message.

Industry observers note that that remarked, guys, please don't waste your one message on "hey girl." "Read her profile and talk to her like a human being," indicates Arrechea. "Not 'hey.' Not a copy-and-pasted pickup line.".

Bumble also has an AI assistant called "Bee," but founder Whitney Wolfe Herd stated on the company's August earnings call that it won't replace swiping. "Let me be clear: Bee is not replacing the swipe. We are not aiming for an AI-driven experience. Bee is simply the intelligence under the hood," she said. She also said bigger profile and IRL updates were coming in early 2027. In the meantime, Bumble added profile badges for "ethical non-monogamy" and "intimacy without commitment," so it's easier to say what you want.

Bumble is trying to get you offline faster. It's testing a "Suggest a Date" feature in Canada so you can skip the endless back-and-forth. In October, it launched "Handles," so you can give someone your @ instead of your phone number. (I love this for when you meet someone cute but aren't ready to hand over your number.) The optional feature is available to verified U.S. iOS users. Someone needs your exact handle to find you, and you still have to like each other before you can chat.

In a recent development, if one-on-one dates aren't your thing, Bumble also debuted "Looks," a standalone app for meeting people IRL in small groups. It's open to anyone 21+, but only in Fresh York City for now. There's also the "Instant Match" QR code, which lets you match with someone you meet at a bar and check whether they're verified before you go home with them.

It has been revealed that I do want to be upfront about Bumble's complications, though. A class-action lawsuit alleges that Bumble failed to protect user data during a "massive" breach by the hacker group ShinyHunters earlier this year. And in October, Bumble announced a $1.3 billion deal to go private. Ithaca Holdings is taking over, and Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman are expected to become co-CEOs. Wolfe Herd is expected to become a strategic adviser and join the board of Bumble's latest parent company, according to a Nov. 20 SEC filing. I'm not sure yet how any of this will change the app.

Recent findings suggest that even with all that going on, Bumble's free version is pretty solid. You can chat by text, voice, or video without paying, and free customers get basic filters like age, distance, and verified profiles. Premium features (Bumble Boost or a premium membership) get you advanced filters, but you don't need them to find a hookup buddy.

Industry observers note that feeld is for the explorers: the singles, couples, and polycules looking to ethically explore non-monogamy, kink, and alternative relationship styles. If you find the binary options on most dating apps to be limiting, Feeld's inclusive, consent-forward environment is refreshing. It’s a hub for people practicing "relationship anarchy" or just curious about connections without traditional rules.

It's worth noting, however, that the app is attracting more "vanilla" consumers (those with conventional tastes) lately, which is changing the dynamic somewhat. But even those "normies" might be hiding a wild side: Feeld's "State of Reflections Volume 1: Am I Normal?" report found that 42 percent of mainstream, non-Feeld daters actually practice kink. And the community is getting more curious by the day.

Sources indicate that being sexually open-minded doesn’t mean you want to skip the buildup. Feeld’s latest “State of Dating” report surveyed 3,310 adults in the U.S. and UK and found that eight in 10 considered anticipation "crucial" to erotic excitement. And 58 percent said authenticity and clear intentions were missing from modern dating. You can want something casual and still want a little sexual tension before someone asks for your address.

It has been revealed that feeld has had its share of bugs, especially after its 2023 relaunch, and some users still report glitches. But nothing else does what it does for the kink community. And even as it gets more mainstream (Forbes reported in October that its revenue rose more than 30 percent in 2025), it's still one of the most sex-positive apps I've used.

The free “Constellation” feature lets you be transparent by linking your profile with up to five partners, and you can use more than 20 labels to define those connections, from "Lover" and "Dom" to "Friend with benefits." (While this feature links your profiles, your private chat histories and existing connections are not shared with your partners.) The app also offers detailed desire and kink tags, from "Bondage" to "Cuddling," so you can find exactly what you're looking for.

Sources indicate that feeld is also rolling out "Expiring connections." If neither of you sends a message within five days of connecting, you'll automatically disconnect, and that person goes back into your Discover feed. I like this one, since it pushes you to say hi before your connections pile up.

"Feeld is a good app for finding hookups because the people on it are sexually open-minded but also conscious," indicates Weiss. "Many of them are looking for casual sexual encounters, but not 'casual' in the sense of wanting to make a conquest or put in minimal effort," she adds. "I often recommend this app to couples who want to find a third person to play with or date, as well as singles who want to explore different sexual fantasies and subcultures.".

Recent findings suggest that to make articulating those desires even easier, Feeld introduced an interactive quiz called "Reflections" that helps you map out your boundaries, relationships, and kink affinities. And according to Feeld’s May 2026 “State of Reflections Volume 2: The Words We Didn’t Have” report, the quiz helped users put those desires into words. After taking the quiz, 72 percent of users noted they changed (or thought about changing) how they communicate their desires on their profiles, and over half felt more empowered to bring up boundaries and safe sex right from the start. Once you finish the quiz, you get a custom link and QR code to share your dealbreakers with potential partners before you even meet.

If you're still figuring out how to put your relationship structure into words, Weiss suggests keeping it playful: "You can write something cute like 'ethical slut' or 'I have room for more than one love of my life in my heart' instead of just using the technical language.".

If you're tired of Tinder, HUD is worth the download, and its tagline is literally "Fun without strings attached." HUD stands for "Honest, Upfront, and Direct," and it's the app for people who aren’t afraid to be their most authentic selves. Translation: If you're into non-monogamy, this is where you'll find like-minded people.

In a recent development, the people on this app aren’t here to find their forever person, but friends with benefits is definitely on the table. You might also find kinksters, ethical non-monogamous folks, and people interested in exploring relationship styles that are a little outside the mainstream. With more than 19 million users worldwide as of 2026, HUD offers many opportunities for your next hookup.

If Hinge and Pure had a baby, it would be HUD. This app doesn’t beat around the bush, but it’s also artsy in presentation and has a kinky-fun community behind it.

Sources indicate that like Hinge, you can answer prompts (up to three), add photos (up to five), and note whether you’re into smoking, drinking, or drugs. There’s also a really cool "My Bedroom" feature that lets you choose three "desires" that you’re really into, three "desires" you’re "open" to, and three you’re definitely not into. Examples include "bondage," "butt stuff," and "golden showers." There are tons of "desires" to choose from, even if you’re not that kinky, so have fun with it.

Speaking of kinky, HUD published its 2026 Pleasure Census, a global culture report in partnership with Girls Get Off. The survey revealed that 80 percent of daters aren't having as much sex as they'd ideally like, and those who openly talk about what they want in bed are three times more likely to reach orgasm with a partner every time. That's why features like "My Bedroom" are so great; they eliminate that awkward barrier to communication before you even meet up.

Besides "My Bedroom," HUD has an "Anti-Commitment Mode" badge you can add to your profile to let potential matches know why you're here. You’ll also get to pick your archetype (if you’re not sure what yours is, the app has a little quiz) to help you find your match. You can even add your favorite song to your profile.

In a recent development, not sure how to explain that you're poly, kinky, or just not looking for anything serious? Keep it short. "You don't need to write a manifesto in your dating bio!" says Paulita Pappel, intimacy expert and founder of Lustery. "The bio is there to open the right door, not to function as a legal contract.".

Recent findings suggest that the chat features are also a little more developed than those in a typical hookup app. You can engage with someone’s profile just by liking or commenting on their prompts, photos, etc. The video chat option also shows both cameras blurred until you both decide to reveal yourselves. Of course, you can get more features with a premium subscription, but the free version offers a lot.

Sources indicate that hily (short for "Hey, I Like You") is for anyone who wants a little more substance than Tinder's fast-swipe format but doesn't want to answer a ton of questions to get set up and start matching. The app gives you total flexibility: you can keep your profile simple, or fill out optional prompts, pick lifestyle passions, and take its 40-question "Icks&Clicks" compatibility quiz to see how compatible you are with potential matches before chatting.

Granted, my experience comes from living in a small Southern town (where more than 1,400 men were active at any given moment), but even compared to testing Hinge in the same spot, Hily brought out a distinct crowd. The user pool was packed with blue-collar guys, hunters, fishers, and dudes on motorcycles looking for low-pressure hangouts, casual flings, or sexting partners. While I didn't run into many queer women (mostly couples looking for a third), if you're looking for straight hookups with outdoorsy or country-leaning guys, the active user base makes finding a match easy.

Read our full review of the Hily dating app.

Industry observers note that even though it doesn't get as much attention as Tinder or Bumble, Hily has over 43 million users and lets you control how much effort you put into your profile. You can pick intentions like "Physical connection" or "Something casual," list up to 12 passions, and answer optional prompts under categories like "My Dating Guide" and "Life Vibes." It also features a "Roulette" wheel that hands out free daily perks like profile boosts and rollbacks.

Recent findings suggest that there are a couple of quirks to keep in mind while browsing, though. While the "Finder" will show you people who match your set filters (like age, location, and gender), those preferences don't necessarily apply to who lands in your "Likes" feed. Plus, anyone who likes your profile stays blurred unless you pay for a subscription — unless you get lucky and win free "Unblurs" from the daily Roulette wheel or happen to stumble across them naturally in the "Finder.".

Industry observers note that if you're not too keen on receiving NSFW photos or chats, Hily added a feature called "Consent Guard." Built with sexologists, this tool scans incoming messages and photos for adult content and gives you a pop-up warning so you can decide whether you actually want to see a nude or explicit text before opening it. It keeps your inbox safe from surprise cyberflashing, but lets you turn up the heat as soon as you give the green light. "[Consent tools] make it less likely for owners to be sexually harassed, while also allowing them to see who the culprits are so they can choose not to engage with them," states Weiss.

In a recent development, while other apps push AI matchmakers, Hily is taking a different approach. Its early 2026 "T.R.U.T.H. Report" showed that nearly 70 percent of daters feel AI matchmakers make dating feel fake. In response, Hily brought back its "HI" (Human Intelligence) campaign to focus on real human chemistry instead of automated matching algorithms.

If you're a gay, bi, trans, or queer man looking for a hookup, Grindr is still where most people start. There are other options out there, but nothing has more guys online at once. According to Grindr's "Unwrapped" report, owners sent over 135 billion chats last year, and the most-searched profile tag was "Hung." (Of course it was.).

In a recent development, the free version isn't perfect, though. In his review, Tyler Schoeber remarked it's "overrun with intrusive ads," and it limits you to about 87 messageable profiles on the grid unless you upgrade. A Grindr XTRA membership can get pricey, too. The good news is that Grindr's 2026 roadmap includes "rewarded ads," which would let free users unlock premium features by watching an ad.

Even with the ads, Grindr is still the go-to hookup app for gay men because so many people use it.

Sources indicate that grindr's location-based grid makes it really easy to see who's nearby and available, which matters even more in smaller towns where the queer community might be limited. This year, Grindr is putting its "Right Now" feature directly on the map, so you can see who's looking to hook up near you. According to Grindr's data from May, Right Now is most popular in places like Taiwan, the Philippines, Lima, Buenos Aires, and Medellín. There's also "Discreet Posting," which lets you post a hookup request without showing your profile until you approve a chat.

Recent findings suggest that aside from getting your biscuit buttered, Grindr has become a hub for travelers. In May, it released the third season of its Host or Travel series, and its "Roam" feature lets you drop a pin anywhere in the world to see who's around before you even get there. Grindr's map is also being updated to show gay bars, clubs, and gyms, and the app is testing direct hotel bookings.

The biggest Grindr news this year is its AI subscription, "Edge." After testing it in a few markets, Grindr debuted Edge worldwide on Nov. 17 for $120 a month or $70 a week in the U.S. It's built on Grindr's own AI, "gAI," and includes daily profile recommendations, a "Reconnect" feature for revisiting past connections, and "Insights" on things like compatibility and how likely someone is to reply. Grindr is also capping Edge at 1 percent of its monthly owners, so not everyone will be able to get it. That's a lot of money for a hookup app, but it's optional, and you can turn off AI-powered features in your privacy settings.

According to recent reports, however, the platform isn't without its complications. In September, it agreed to pay £26 million (about $35 million) to settle a U.K. class-action lawsuit alleging it shared users' HIV status and other sensitive data with third parties before 2020. Grindr disputes the claims, didn't admit liability, and says it has overhauled its privacy practices since then. People have also criticized its content moderation as inconsistent, like when it went back and forth on banning "no Zionists" in profiles in 2025.

That remarked, Grindr has added a lot of safety features lately. Last year, it publicly supported the "App Store Accountability Act," which would have Apple or Google handle age verification at the device level, so you don't have to upload your ID to every app. It also added an in-app Safety Center and a "Taken on Grindr" timestamp that demonstrates how recent someone's photos are. And through its Grindr for Equality initiative, it rolled out sexual health features like automated HIV testing reminders, status sharing, and PrEP and DoxyPEP profile options.

On Nov. 2, Grindr also finished acquiring Freddie, an online healthcare service that specializes in HIV prevention. If you're in the U.S. or Canada, you can use Freddie through Grindr's Health section to talk to a clinician, get tested, and get PrEP (medication that helps prevent HIV) delivered discreetly.

The ads are annoying, and the paid tiers add up fast. But for quick, location-based hookups, Grindr is still king.

Sources indicate that HER was created by and for queer women, so you can meet women and nonbinary folks without worrying about "skeevy guys" sexualizing you. It launched in 2015, and while it isn't built just for hookups, it's a great place to find something casual (or something more, if that's what happens). It also has more than 15 million users, so there are plenty of people to meet.

From my own experience, HER still works. I met a really sweet girl in Nashville on HER, and we went on a few dates. So for now, it's still my top recommendation for queer women.

HER makes it easy to say what you want. The "Looking for" section on your profile lets you add a "something casual" tag that everyone can see. HER also added "Feelings," temporary tags like "Hook up" or "Flirty" that you can add to your profile to show what you're in the mood for right now.

It has been revealed that the app works a lot like a social media platform. There's a social feed, events, and media for the LGBTQ+ community. The interface can feel a little clunky at first, but it's not hard to figure out. For safety, HER offers photo verification, so verified profiles get a checkmark badge.

According to recent reports, in 2025, Match Group bought HER, and a lot of consumers weren't happy about it. Many people on Reddit worried it would lead to the "enshittification" of another queer platform they love. HER founder Robyn Exton said she was optimistic, and Match Group CEO Spencer Rascoff promised to "protect" what makes the app special. Now we're all just waiting to see if they actually do.

So far, the app's main features haven't really changed. HER started the year with a "Sapphic Restart" campaign about putting its community first. And it hasn't gotten any less horny, either. Its "Everything Reminds Me of HER" billboards in Latest York and Los Angeles were full of sexy innuendos, like champagne pouring over skin and fingers slipping into a bowling ball. They went viral on TikTok and Instagram because, of course, they did.

Sniffies is a web-based cruising platform built for one thing: finding sex, right now, with minimal small talk. Sniffies was deemed too hardcore for the App Store, and so it's not technically an app. It's a hookup destination for men seeking men who want spontaneous and anonymous encounters.

The vibe is explicit and unapologetically focused on sex, so don't come here looking for a long-term relationship. While it's free to use and focused on anonymity, paid Sniffies users get additional privacy features for extra peace of mind.

Read our full review of Sniffies.

If you feel like Tinder and Grindr aren't direct enough, I'd like to introduce you to Sniffies, the hookup platform that brings cruising into the 21st century. It released an official iOS app in March 2025, only to be kicked out of the App Store by May for being, well, too horny for Apple. But if you downloaded the app before it was removed, and haven't deleted it, it should still work.

As soon as you enter the website, you'll see a map of guys nearby who are looking for action in your area. (You don't have to deal with registering for an account or anything — pull up the site, choose to browse anonymously, complete the age verification and captcha, and you're in.) The "Cruiser Filters" let you search for exactly what you're into, from body type to endowment size to your favorite sex positions.

In April, Sniffies added a few updates to make finding someone even faster. "Cruiser Cards" is a scrollable carousel that highlights active guys nearby so you don't have to hunt around the map. They’ve also added a upcoming "Into Filter" and "Position Icons" that put a cruiser’s intent and favorite sex positions directly on their map avatar.

Recent findings suggest that when you're ready to meet, you can use the new "Share a Spot" feature to drop a temporary, expiring map pin directly into the chat. It’s much better than sending vague directions or swapping apps to share your location. They even added "Share a Group," which lets you send live group event details — like the time and who’s attending. And if you're planning a trip, "Travel Mode" lets you cruise another neighborhood or city before you get there. It's a Sniffies PLUS feature.

In a recent development, it's also totally free to use, but a premium membership (Sniffies PLUS, which costs $9.99 a month) will get you perks like unlimited messaging, ad-free browsing, extra privacy, and read receipts. In fact, while competitors like Grindr are taking heat for putting basic features behind a paywall, Sniffies' CMO Eli Martin recently stated they're focused on building tools that make connection easier without upsells, and it's working.

According to recent reports, the app now has around three million monthly active customers who send 20 million messages daily, and has even caught Match Group's attention. The company invested $100 million in Sniffies in April, a deal that also gives Match an option to buy the platform outright. On a November earnings call, Match Group CEO Spencer Rascoff said the company now owns "about half" of Sniffies.

In a recent development, if your idea of a perfect match is someone who can talk about the nuances of rope suspension one minute and be Dungeon Master for your next D&D night the next, you should probably be on FetLife. Just know that FetLife is a social network for the kink community, not a typical hookup app, so people might not appreciate it if you treat it like a swiping app. Still, it's the place online for established kinksters, which makes it great for meeting sexy new friends who share your very specific interests.

In a recent development, it's also my go-to for gamers. There isn't a hookup app made just for gamers that I'd recommend, but FetLife has a lot of self-described nerds, and there's a surprising amount of overlap between the gaming and kink communities.

"FetLife is popular among gamers and even has some subgroups specifically for kinky gamers," notes Weiss. "The app/site tends to attract nerds and other fringe communities.".

If you're nervous about making the first move, there's "Crushing On," which FetLife added in April. You can privately mark that you have a crush on someone, and they won't be notified. If they mark you too, FetLife lets you both know at the same time, so you can start a conversation from there.

OkCupid (removed October 2026): OkCupid is still worth considering for values-driven dating, but I prefer Feeld, HUD, and HER for this hookup-focused list. The FTC’s 2026 action against OkCupid, over allegations that it shared nearly 3 million owners’ photos and other personal information with facial recognition company Clarifai in 2014, also raised privacy concerns I couldn’t ignore.

Hily (added August 2026): I’ve added Hily to our top picks because its free tier is surprisingly generous (up to 100 likes a day!) and its AI safety tech (like Consent Guard) makes it a standout option for casual, blunt daters looking for a fresh alternative to the Significant Three.

According to recent reports, you might notice a few apps that pop up in ads or other lists are missing here. That’s intentional. I swipe through the good, the bad, and the downright sketchy so you don’t have to. For an app to make my list, it has to offer more than a convincing ad.

Here's a shortlist of apps that didn't make the cut:.

Plenty of Fish: POF's rebrand didn't do it any favors. My last round of testing showed it removed key features like free messaging with non-matches, and I kept running into the same old profiles. (Removed January 2025.).

Recent findings suggest that match: Some people swear they've found casual hookups on Match, but that's not what it's for. It's still one of my top picks for a long-term relationship. For a hookup? You're fishing in the wrong pond. (Removed August 2025.).

It has been revealed that wild: You’ve probably seen ads for this one. On paper, Wild sounds like the perfect casual dating app. In practice, the paywalls are aggressive, the distance filter doesn't work, and you have to pay for anything that's even remotely useful. Unless you're willing to spend serious cash upfront (and hope for the best), the experience feels more limited than with more generous free options like Tinder or Hily.

In a recent development, DOWN: This app (formerly "Bang With Friends") is known for its simple "Get Down" vs. "Get Date" feature. It sounds clever, but in reality, the experience is messy at best. Many people report feeling scammed by subscriptions that don't deliver matches, or finding that the few real people on there are... let's say "odd." It’s hard to recommend an app when the main user complaint is "Is anyone real?" Hard pass.

It has been revealed that facebook Dating: Yes, Facebook has a dating section, and it’s surprisingly massive (and completely free, which is huge). While it's a decent option for casual dating, the vibe tends to be a bit more "friends of friends" and "relationship-focused" than the anonymous, no-strings energy you get from apps like Pure or Feeld. (For Mashable's Chance Townsend, signing up was "the most uneventful dating experience" of his life.) It's also added an AI dating assistant and "Meet Cute," which sends you one surprise match a week. It's worth a shot if you're already on Facebook, but it didn't quite crack my top tier for no-strings-attached hookups specifically.

Tinder is still the best hookup app for most people. Pure is worth trying if you want a more discreet profile, while Feeld is where I’d go for kink or ethical non-monogamy. For queer men, there’s Grindr or Sniffies; for queer women, HER.

Tinder lets you match and chat for free, Hinge indicates your incoming likes one at a time, and I got up to 100 "likes" a day on Hily’s free version.

Pure is the best anonymous hookup app. You don’t have to put your real name on your profile, and chats disappear after 24 hours unless you both agree to keep them.

It has been revealed that bumble is worth considering. Either person can send the first message, but they can’t keep sending messages unless the recipient replies. Pure is worth trying if you want to be direct about your turn-ons, while HER is my top pick for queer women.

Feeld is where I’d start. “I often recommend this app to couples who want to find a third person to play with or date,” says Weiss. Say whether you’re dating together or separately and what you’re hoping to find. If you’re fresh to non-monogamy, have the boundaries conversation with your partner before involving someone else.

It has been revealed that no app can guarantee your safety. Look for tools that give you control over who can contact you, what they can send, and how much personal information they can see.

Photo or face verification: Tinder’s Face Check uses a video selfie to help check that someone matches their profile photos. Bumble also offers photo verification and lets you ask a match to verify their photos.

Nude filters: Pure’s My Media Rules and Hily's Consent Guard let you block or screen explicit content before opening it. Bumble’s Private Detector automatically blurs potentially explicit photos, so you can decide whether to view them.

Date sharing: Pure’s Safety Signal lets you share your last-known location and date details with a trusted friend. Tinder’s Share My Date and Bumble’s Share Date let you share looks, including who you’re meeting, where, and when.

Blocking and reporting: Never use an app that makes it hard to report bad behavior. Bumble, for example, lets you block and report someone from their profile or chat without telling them who reported them.

In a recent development, meet in a public place first, get yourself there and home, and tell a friend where you’ll be. “Casual sex does not require casual safety,” says Hatton. “Do not give a stranger your home address simply because the intention of the connection is casual.” Weiss also recommends having a friend check in later that night or the next morning.

They push boundaries you've already set.

They pressure you to drink or host immediately.

They pressure you to move off the app before you’re comfortable.

Sources indicate that be honest and specific about what you want, like “Looking for a regular FWB” or your specific kinks if you’re on Feeld. You don’t need to spell out every detail. “The bio is there to open the right door, not to function as a legal contract,” indicates Pappel.

Sometimes, but try the free version first. If you keep running into limits on profiles, filters, or messages, an upgrade might be worth it. A short subscription can also make sense for a trip — that’s when Tyler Schoeber recommends paying in his Grindr XTRA review. If you’re not interested in anyone you’re seeing, I wouldn’t rush to pay.

Here’s what I look for when testing hookup apps, from what you can do for free to how much control you have over who can contact you.

Recent findings suggest that hands-on testing: I create profiles on every app or site in this guide, including browser-based options like Sniffies. I check how easy it is to find people who want something casual, which features are free, and what’s locked behind a subscription.

Recent findings suggest that privacy and tech checks: I also look at privacy settings, verification, and blocking and reporting tools. When I try AI features, I consider whether they’re useful or just another reason to charge you more.

In a recent development, expert and community feedback: User reviews and Reddit threads help me compare my experience with other people’s. I also consulted the following experts about communicating intentions, setting boundaries, and meeting offline:.

Suzannah Weiss, sex/couples therapist and resident sexologist for Erojoy.

Sandra Hatton, professional matchmaker and founder of When We First.

Erica Arrechea, founder and CEO of Cinqe Matchmaking.

Caroline Millet, dating burnout coach and former matchmaker.

Paulita Pappel, intimacy expert and founder of Lustery.

Alexander Liebisch, CEO and founder of TinderProfile.ai.

Michelle Herzog, LMFT, and AASECT-certified sex therapist.

Continuous monitoring: When updating this guide, I check for changes to pricing, features, and availability and reconsider which apps belong on the list.

It has been revealed that tabitha Britt is an award-winning freelance journalist, editor, and SEO/AEO strategist. Aside from reviewing dating apps and sex toys for Mashable, Tabitha is also the founding editor-in-chief of DO YOU ENDO — a digital magazine by individuals with endometriosis, for individuals with endometriosis. She has a Master's degree in Creative Publishing and Critical Journalism from The Fresh School for Social Research and is a grad of Sextech School. You can find more of her work in various online publications, including National Geographic, Glamour, Better Homes & Gardens, and Everyday Health.

Industry observers note that the Dell XPS 13 was already a great deal, with its aggressive starting price and beautiful display. And then comes along this discount, which brings the price down to just $550. A laptop this premium for under $600 feels outrageous, even if it only comes with 8 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage. If you’re using this for work or school, you might want to consider the upgraded 16-GB model, which is also on sale for Black Friday. There’s no laptop deal quite like it right now. —Luke Larsen.

Gaming laptops have gotten really expensive over the past year—to the point where I could no longer recommend any of the available options around $1,000. This deal gets close though, bringing it down to its cheapest price ever. It’s almost unheard of to find a gaming laptop with an RTX 5060 at this price, especially since this also comes with a terabyte of storage. This is a chunky boy at almost an inch thick, but hey, that’s not uncommon for gaming laptops in this price range. —Luke Larsen.

Recent findings suggest that I don’t normally recommend two-year-old laptops. But this is the cheapest price the Surface Laptop has dropped to this entire year, making it worth buying again. Personally, I love the 3:2 aspect ratio, which gives it a taller form factor than standard laptops. And beyond that, it’s one of the most premium-feeling laptops you can buy on the Windows side. I should note that this one isn’t the latest version with the newer chips, but for $900, it’s still great. Just know that you’re only getting 256 GB of storage. —Luke Larsen.

According to recent reports, I’ve often called the MacBook Air the laptop most people should buy. Even after testing dozens of upcoming laptops this year, I stand by that statement. It balances price, battery life, performance, and quality in a way that’s still unbeaten by the competition. The only problem is that at its retail price of $1,299, it’s been a bit too expensive. At a full $250 off, though, it’s a must-buy. —Luke Larsen.

As Apple’s entry-level laptop, the MacBook Neo hasn’t seen much of a sale since it came out this spring. But finally, the MacBook Neo is down $50 to just $649. While its direct competitor, the XPS 13, is cheaper, the Neo is the cheapest way into the macOS ecosystem, even though you’ll have to live with only 8 GB of RAM. —Luke Larsen.

In a recent development, the Mac Mini has recently become a surprise hot product, primarily thanks to the surge of interest in running AI models locally. The Mac Mini works quite well as an affordable, always-on AI box for your home, especially if you upgrade it to at least 32 GB of RAM. In terms of price, this has been the standard discount that Amazon has been offering for the past month or so, but that doesn’t mean it’s not still a strong value. —Luke Larsen.

The Mac Studio is a monster, but as you can tell by the price, it’s solely for creative pros and AI enthusiasts. The most powerful M5 Ultra model isn’t on sale, but you can take $200 off the M5 Max model, which still comes with 36 GB of RAM. Whether you’re a video editor or wanting an at-home, all-powerful AI box for coding, the Mac Studio is an absolute champ. —Luke Larsen.

The base iPad is the one we recommend most people buy when shopping for a tablet. This particular discount isn’t out of the ordinary, but it’s still a competitive price for what you get. This isn’t the iPad to get for work, but you don’t want to pay more just to take notes, play games, and leisurely scroll. If that’s primarily what you want an iPad for, this is the one you want. —Luke Larsen.

This is the previous-gen iPad Mini, so it doesn’t have the OLED screen and faster performance of the newer model. But if you’re just looking for a simple small tablet for reading books and playing games, the newer model might be overkill anyways—especially given the price. —Luke Larsen.

Industry observers note that if you need an iPad that can double for work on the go, the iPad Air is the one to get. The discount here is fairly standard, though it’s still $100 off the retail price you’d pay when buying directly through Apple. Whether you opt for the 11-inch or 13-inch screen, make sure to pair it with a Magic Keyboard attachment for the full iPad experience. —Luke Larsen.

This is a great price for AirPods Pro 3, our de facto wireless earbud of choice for anyone with an iPhone. They are stacked with some of the best automated noise-canceling and transparency modes you can get in wireless earbuds, plus other useful features like accurate heart rate tracking (so you can track workout data without a fitness tracker) and live translation. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Industry observers note that look, we see this price often for AirPods Max 2 whenever there is a massive sale event. But anything to lower their crazy $550 MSRP is noteworthy, considering how great (and popular) they are for Apple fans. They have some of the best noise-canceling and transparency modes around, plus a clear, detailed sound profile that puts wireless earbuds to shame. —Harry Rabinowitz.

It has been revealed that topping my guide of the best mesh Wi-Fi systems, the Wi-Fi 7 Netgear Orbi 770 Series is perfect for most families. It’s a tri-band mesh (2.4-, 5-, and 6-GHz) offering simple setup, stable and speedy internet connectivity, and expansive coverage. The stylish tower design is unobtrusive, the internal antennas ensure your whole home gets online, and it delivers the benefits of Wi-Fi 7, including MLO (Multi-Link Operation) to enable Wi-Fi 7 devices to connect on multiple bands at once. —Simon Hill.

According to recent reports, for folks with an Eero mesh looking to boost that backyard Wi-Fi, the Eero Outdoor 7 is a weatherproof dual-band Wi-Fi 7 router that extends coverage into your garden. Buy a pair, and you can set up a point-to-point connection to deliver up to hundreds of megabits per second, up to a half-mile away. Ideal if you need Wi-Fi in a distant barn, garage, or other outbuilding, or at the bottom of a massive yard. This is the lowest price I’ve seen for this. —Simon Hill.

This router will cover most homes and apartments up to around 2,000 square feet, with fast and reliable connectivity, and tops our best Wi-Fi routers guide. It’s only dual-band, so you miss out on the 6-GHz band, but you get all the other advantages of Wi-Fi 7. It also has a generous array of ports and comes with free security software and parental controls. Support for VPN service, separate IoT or guest networks, and AiMesh rounds out an excellent device. —Simon Hill.

Sources indicate that standing desks are often quite expensive, which is to be expected. But this is one of the few affordable standing desks worth buying. It comes in a number of different sizes, colors, and styles, and the laminated top protects against spills. It’s not the simplest to set up, but as our testers have verified, the FlexiSpot EN1 makes up for it by being such an affordable upgrade to your home office ergonomics. —Luke Larsen.

Keychron is our favorite brand of keyboards, but they tend to be expensive. This is the best option in the lineup that’s actually quite affordable. Despite being cheaper, it still has a lot of the hallmarks of Keychron’s keyboards, including the hot-swappable switches, retro design, and high-end build quality. —Luke Larsen.

Sources indicate that there’s no mouse as beloved as Logitech’s MX Master line, primarily known for its comfortable grip, customization, and quality. The latest model makes a number of small tweaks to improve the mouse even further, including intuitive gesture controls and haptic feedback. If you take your work seriously, the MX Master 4 will be an excellent inclusion in your home office setup. —Luke Larsen.

I’m still astounded that you can buy a high-quality 4K monitor for such little money these days. The Dell 27 Plus is my top pick as the monitor most people should buy, and the fact that it’s nearly $200 only bolsters that recommendation even more. The only compromise is that it’s a bit limited in terms of ports, but you can upgrade to the S2725DC with USB ports. —Luke Larsen.

It has been revealed that if you want an office chair that’s truly premium, the Steelcase Gesture is our recommendation. It’s a comfortable, attractive chair that comes in multiple colors, and you’ll find different sale prices for those different colors if you have a preference. It looks elegant, has a nice cushy seat, and you can adjust the lumbar support with the built-in tabs. —Nena Farrell.

We’ve liked a few different Staples chairs over the years for a great office chair under $200, and while the Staples Dexley is our current pick (at the moment on sale too, but only $10 off), the Staples Hyken has a better deal. It’s down to $128, and it’s a good pick over the Dexley if you’re shorter. These seats both have great airflow and include a headrest. —Nena Farrell.

Sources indicate that created from fabric scraps that would otherwise end up in a landfill, this thoughtfully constructed bag looks great and can carry everything you need for a weeklong trip. WIRED's Gear team has loved this bag for almost a decade now, and it's still one of our favorites. The pack straps and adjustable waist belt all tuck away neatly when you don't need them, turning this Allpa into more of a soft suitcase. —Scott Gilbertson.

According to recent reports, the Coraza is a gorgeous suitcase, and thanks to Cotopaxi's emphasis on ethical business, it's our top pick for the most sustainable carry on. Latched hard-shell luggage like the Coraza offers many of the benefits of an aluminum roller, but without the weight or the cost. If you want to upgrade your luggage without breaking the bank, the Coraza is a great choice. —Scott Gilbertson.

Industry observers note that cotopaxi’s trim, colorful little bag swallows those odds and ends that would otherwise be careening around lose in your larger bag. It’s made from light recycled deadstock nylon and weighs in at a modest 6.5 ounces. The recycled fabric means your bag will be unique and the 4-liter capacity spread over three different compartments, gives you some organizational options. —Scott Gilbertson.

Everything at Away Luggage is 25 percent off right now, including the Softside Carry-On, our top pick among roller bags. Multiple WIRED staffers own the hard-sided carry-on (at the moment $206 ($69 off) because it's good-looking and reasonably priced. However, former senior commerce editor Adrienne So prefers the brand's Softside Carry-On because it highlights scuffs less easily, won't crack, and is more flexible if you overpack. —Scott Gilbertson.

The Everywhere Tote is our favorite travel tote. Made from water-resistant nylon and accented with leather trim, I take the Everywhere Tote everywhere. It's the handbag you reach for when you're commuting, planning an overnight stay, or catching a flight. —Boutayna Chokrane.

Gear editor Julian Chokkattu tests dozens of camera bags, and this roll-top model is his all-time favorite. Wandrd's popular Prvke (pronounced "provoke") now has zippered access to the rolltop, a larger side-access opening, and more internal organization. It's plenty roomy and well-sealed against the elements to protect your camera gear. —Scott Gilbertson.

Recent findings suggest that the Sony XM4C are finally on sale, and all is right in the world. These are essentially a version two of the cult-classic Sony WH-1000XM4, one of our favorite headphones of 2020, and one of Sony’s best-selling headphones ever. They are really the people’s choice: excellent sound, great noise-canceling (though not as good as Bose’s), a comfortable fit, a folding design, on-ear detection, and decent battery life, all at a reasonable price. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Recent findings suggest that with these and the Sony XM4C both at $200 for Black Friday, we’re spoiled for choice. In my review of the Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), my main gripe was price—these are great headphones that float in a strange price point between midrange and premium. That concern flies out the window with this excellent discount. They are supremely comfortable and have some of the best noise-canceling on the market—unmatched at this deal price of $200. —Harry Rabinowitz.

In a recent development, the lowest price to date on my favorite pair of wireless earbuds? Sign me up. I lauded the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro in my review because they punch way above their price point, giving much pricier earbuds a run for their money. But it’s call quality that blew me away: I sound better on these earbuds than any other I’ve tested, by far. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Recent findings suggest that finally, a good sale on the Sony WH-1000XM6. This is the lowest price ever for arguably the best noise-canceling headphones you can buy. They go toe-to-toe with Bose for the best noise-canceling around, have a folding, travel-friendly design, and sound absolutely stellar. They set the bar for over-ear headphones, and remain one of the pairs I test others against when writing reviews. —Harry Rabinowitz.

In a recent development, our former top pick for best open earbuds, this pair was replaced only by its successor, the AeroClip 2. It’s also at its lowest price ever (by a lot). These open earbuds wrap around your outer ear, leaving your inner ear open to hear the world around you. They’re comfortable, water- and dust-resistant, and have excellent battery life, meaning you can wear them for outdoor exercise; a rainy dog walk; or anything, really. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Industry observers note that these are the best ANC earbuds, full stop. They have the strongest automated noise-canceling of any earbuds I’ve tested—Latest York City streets and busy cafes became a dim hum with ANC on. They also sound great, with clear, detailed instrumentation on some of my favorite albums. —Harry Rabinowitz.

According to recent reports, this is probably the standout TV deal this Black Friday, if the price holds. The LG C6 has been at its lowest price ever since November started, making it the best OLED TV deal around. We’re still testing it, but early impressions are positive, just like they were for the C5 and C4 before it. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Art TVs act as decent televisions plus convincingly realistic wall art, and Samsung’s The Frame is the leader in the category. This 2025 model has an excellent matte, anti-reflective-coated display that makes paintings and wall art look textured and surprisingly realistic. Do note that Samsung only offers 30 free art images—you'll need a $5 monthly subscription to the Samsung Art Store to access the full catalog of over 5,000. —Harry Rabinowitz.

One of the best budget TVs at its lowest price ever. Really, getting picture quality that’s this good for under $1,000 is just silly. The TCL QM7L is bright, colorful, and detailed, according to WIRED contributor Rick Broida. Even the built-in speakers ain’t half-bad (though we still recommend getting a soundbar). —Harry Rabinowitz.

It has been revealed that another great budget TV at its lowest price ever for Black Friday. Former WIRED reviewer Ryan Waniata highlighted the Hisense U7SG’s very high brightness and clear picture quality, especially for its price point. It comes in two versions: one with Google TV built in and one with Fire TV. (We prefer [and linked to] the Google TV model.) —Harry Rabinowitz.

Sources indicate that the Roku Pro Series OLED is our favorite budget OLED TV, on sale for the first time ever this Black Friday. It’s one of the lowest-priced OLEDs you can get, and comes with Roku’s easy-to-use operating system (and remote), so it’s a great option for non-techy people looking to try out an OLED screen. The main downside here is that it isn’t as bright as other non-OLED (or pricier OLED) options. —Harry Rabinowitz.

According to recent reports, here’s the thing: Like many consumer tech companies, Roku raised prices significantly across its product lines. The Black Friday sale price for the Streaming Stick Plus With Voice Remote—our favorite streaming device for most people—was the same as the previous regular price. You once could have gotten this device for $20. Still, it’s a simple yet fantastic way to access streaming content on your TV, with support for tons of apps and easy navigation. And the current sale price makes it more palatable than the upcoming MSRP. —Les Shu.

Simply the best all-in-one soundbar. If you want to upgrade your TV audio with one speaker, and not mess around with subwoofers or surround sound, just get the Sonos Arc Ultra. It delivers substantial, wide, and accurate sound across movies, TV shows, and music. While it’s a bit long, it’s not very tall, so it’s easy to fit in front of most TVs without blocking them. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Recent findings suggest that I used this soundbar for years. It’s one of the best compact, not-too-expensive models you can get. And it’s at its lowest price ever for Black Friday, likely spurred on by the release of the newly introduced (not on sale) Sonos Beam Ultra. The Gen 2 (along with the Bose TV Speaker [2nd Gen]) is the soundbar I recommend to people who are tight on space and just want something that works. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Recent findings suggest that this soundbar plus subwoofer is a fantastic way to upgrade your TV audio system for a reasonable price, especially with this discount. It’s one of our favorite soundbars because it’s simple, easy to use, sounds great, adds plenty of bass, and doesn’t cost an arm and a leg. As long as you're not dreaming of upgrading to a multi-speaker surround sound system, this will serve you well. —Harry Rabinowitz.

Industry observers note that one of our favorite cordless vacuums, the V15 Detect is an oldie but a goodie. It's a great Dyson vacuum that was our top pick for a long time because it's more affordable than the Gen5Detect and V16, but still comes with two cleaner heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpet and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) and has 240 air-watts of suction (almost 100 more than the V10 Konical and other cheaper Dyson vacuums). —Nena Farrell.

According to recent reports, if you want a powerful stick vacuum, you don’t have to spend that much—at least, not on Black Friday. The Shark PowerDetect is a fantastic vacuum that performs just as well (sometimes better!) as more expensive Dyson vacuums in my tests, and it works great for picking up everything you can think of off carpets, rugs, and hard floors alike, though I think it’s best for carpets and rugs. You can get it on sale alone, or bundled with a self-emptying base station that will keep the vacuum charged (well worth the upgrade!) —Nena Farrell.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for a new cordless vacuum but want to spend as little as possible (without buying garbage), you’re in luck: Our favorite affordable stick vacuum, the Bissell PowerClean, is on sale, making it even cheaper. It’s a great vacuum that stands upright, has HEPA filtration, and has four lights on the head to help illuminate dust and debris. You’ll get a crevice tool, a small upholstery tool, and a wall mount. —Nena Farrell.

It has been revealed that the best robot vacuum I've tested is also for sale at one of the best prices I've seen it for. The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal is smarter than most vacuums I've tested, thanks to its UV light that helps it find stains around your floors. It does a great job with corner cleaning (nailing my trickiest of corners in my tests) and navigating around my home, though it only can learn a single map, so it's not as ideal for multi-floor homes. But you can just do what my best friend did: buy one for each floor. At this price, you're almost getting it for two for one anyways. —Nena Farrell.

The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is one of my favorite affordable robot vacuums, especially when it’s on sale, and this is the lowest price you’ll find it for. Roborock’s vacuums have fantastic navigation and an easy-to-use app, and overall do a great job cleaning. The Qrevo 2 Pro especially impressed me with its extendable mop arm, which helps it get under cabinets and clean corners around the house. —Nena Farrell.

If you want the cheapest option for a robot vacuum while still getting good quality and mopping, Eufy’s Omni C28 did a great job cleaning multiple floors in my home, making it my overall favorite affordable vacuum pick to this day. For such a well-priced vacuum, it never got lost while navigating my home (a more expensive Eufy vacuum actually did get lost on me, funny enough) and can learn multiple maps if you need to clean more than one floor. It’s often on sale in the $400 range, so this price is the best I’ve seen. —Nena Farrell.

This is the automatic litter box I recommend for anyone who wants a super-cheap, self-cleaning option without extra luxe features like a connected app or built-in camera. It has a familiar open-top design that most cats take to easily, and you control its functions with three buttons on the box: clean, refill litter, and power on/off. If you don’t want to break the bank but want to spend less time scooping urine and stool, I recommend this budget model. —Molly Higgins.

This automatic litter box has an open, front-facing entrance and sits slightly raised on legs. It connects to Wi-Fi, so you can review your cat’s visits in the phone app. Each entry highlights the time, your cat’s weight, and how long the visit lasted. During testing, it was easy to assemble and worked well—we think it’s worth considering, especially at a discount. —Molly Higgins.

This pet water fountain is perfect for cats who love drinking from faucets. It features all-stainless-steel construction, which makes it more hygienic and keeps water colder. The tall spigot is great for cats who love long streams of water, and activated carbon filters sit below the steel top. Plus, the top has a reservoir, so water is always available. It's not app-connected, but the small window lets you easily monitor water levels. —Molly Higgins.

The Kindle Paperwhite is the best of Amazon’s e-readers to buy thanks to its larger screen and warm front light, plus 16 GB of storage. The cheaper base Kindle doesn’t have any of these and loses an inch of screen space. There’s a upcoming Kindle Paperwhite out as of late October, but only the older model is on sale. Don’t worry—you aren’t missing out on much; I recommend buying the on-sale model over the newest one, since the 12th gen is only two years old and still great. —Nena Farrell.

If you want the best e-reader that isn’t a Kindle (and the best-priced colorful e-reader, Kindle or not), the answer is a Kobo, specifically the Kobo Libra Colour. This e-reader has a 7-inch screen, built-in page-turn buttons, and a warm front light, and can be paired with the Kobo stylus so that it doubles as a digital notebook. It had a price hike earlier this year, raising it from $230 to $260, so this price isn’t a great deal compared to what it used to cost, but it’s better to buy it now than pay the new, higher price. —Nena Farrell.

Recent findings suggest that so far, this is my favorite deal you can find on a Kindle. I love using a Kindle Scribe as both an e-reader and a digital notebook, especially since it has a nice long battery life and easy-to-use software. I usually recommend the older, second-gen model since it’s cheaper and has most of the same features, but the third-gen Kindle Scribe is now on sale for less than the older one, so it makes sense to upgrade and pay less. My kind of Black Friday deal. —Nena Farrell.

Amazon (Marker Plus and Folio Bundle).

If you want the best digital notebook with all the bells and whistles, the ReMarkable Paper Pro is ReMarkable’s colorful and most powerful digital notebook yet. It offers one of the best writing experiences if you want a digital notebook that really feels like writing on paper, with a color screen and a gentle front light. Better yet, the bundle on sale will include the Marker Plus with an eraser and a protective folio. ReMarkable’s devices are rarely on sale, so don’t wait on this deal. —Nena Farrell.

Industry observers note that if you want a tablet focused on taking notes but not necessarily a digital notebook with an e-paper screen, the TCL Note A1 Nxtpaper is what you’re looking for. It gives you most of what we like about digital notebook devices, with software focused on note-taking, but it still works as an Android tablet so you can stream videos and use it like a regular tablet. —Nena Farrell.

Every time blenders come up on our team, someone has to mention my personal Vitamix 5200, which I bought refurbished in 2015 (for more than this sale price!) and have used near-daily for the past 11 years. So, here is an update: Yes, it is still going. The plastic carafe suffered a crack, which didn’t affect its function, but I was able to find a replacement via Buy Nothing. Three hundred dollars is an absolute steal for a top-performing blender you will likely only have to buy once in your life. —Kat Merck.

I don’t love that this device markets itself as a “composter” when it really just grinds and dries your food scraps, but it’s the best one I’ve found under $300. It’s got a digital touchscreen and a clear lid so you can keep an eye on the contents; after it goes through its process, your food scraps will be odorless and largely shelf-stable. —Kat Merck.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking to grow lettuce, tomatoes, or even peppers indoors this winter, this tabletop hydroponic system is the best value out there. There are no proprietary pods, so you can grow whatever seeds you’d like (sponge refills are cheap), and the lights and pump are easy to control and monitor from either the unit itself or Letpot’s app. I had an LPH-SE growing chard in my dining room for almost a year, and other than some app bugginess, it performed just as well as the more expensive brands. —Kat Merck.

Recent findings suggest that planning on cooking your holiday roast in the oven or on the smoker? You will need this, our favorite wireless meat thermometer with a display. WIRED contributing reviewer Sal Vaglica tested most major brands for speed, accuracy, and connectivity, and Typhur’s came out on top for its power and ability to notify you when it’s lost connection. Former reviewer Matthew Korfhage also gave it props for its reliability. —Kat Merck.

Industry observers note that WIRED operations manager Scott Gilbertson, former reviewer Matthew Korfhage, and I all use and love cast iron pans from Field. If traditional cast iron is too heavy for you but lighter-weight carbon steel is too temperature-variable, this brand may be your answer. This cookware is just as maneuverable and light as stainless steel yet 100 percent cast iron, with all the heat protection, durability, and nonstick seasoning the material is known for. —Kat Merck.

Industry observers note that what’s the point of owning a home if you can’t have a backyard pizza oven? The Solo Stove Pi Prime is one of our favorite outdoor pizza ovens and a strong option if you want a gas variant. Besides pizza, the opening can accommodate cast-iron pans for other foods (steaks, anybody?), and it has good wind shielding. —Les Shu.

The Technivorm Moccamaster KBGT Coffee Machine is drip coffee perfection. Pair it with good-quality, freshly ground beans, and you’ll have a perfect pot in precisely six minutes. This classic design has been handmade in the Netherlands since 1968, with a steel construction, a copper heating element, and a glass-lined thermal carafe. I love a good e-reader, and Black Friday is one of the best times to buy a newly introduced one. I've scoured the internet and my own guides to find the best Black Friday Kindle and e-reader deals on devices that are worth buying at full price, making these sales something you shouldn't miss if you're in the market for a new e-reader (or want to gift one to someone!).

It has been revealed that great e-readers have e-paper screens that are easier on your eyes than reading on a smartphone or tablet screen, but allow you to bring hundreds of books with you without worrying about damaging any book spines (or your own spine from carrying so many books around). You can connect these to the Libby app to get library ebooks, too, letting your reading run wild and literally free.

Updated November 28, 2026: We've added the Xteink Pocket E-Reader deal to this story, and updated links with current pricing.

According to recent reports, the best all-around Kindle is consistently the Kindle Paperwhite. Right now, only the older 12thgeneration that came out in 2024 is on sale. It's not all that old, and it comes with a larger 7-inch screen, a warm front light, and 16 GB of storage. It's also down to $130, which is a great price for the Paperwhite features. The Paperwhite used to cost $160, but a $30 discount off the original price makes this a deal worth shopping.

If you want a color Kindle, the best choice is the older version. The first-generation Kindle has a massive discount, bringing it down to nearly the same as the Paperwhite's original price tag. Paying $170 for a color screen is a worthy upgrade if you'd like a digital bookshelf full of colorful covers, and that includes no lock-screen ads, a feature you'll have to pay extra for on the Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite. It has everything else we like about the Paperwhite with a warm front light and 7-inch screen, but it does have a shorter battery life (eight weeks is still pretty great, though).

I usually prefer the older Kindle Scribe due to the price tag, but right now, I'd choose the newest model. The third-generation Kindle Scribe is down to $350 from $500, making it cheaper to buy than the $400 second-gen version. I love the updated homepage that brings both my notes and books into one place, making it easy to jump back into whichever I prefer. There are also some AI features for both my notes and books, but I prefer not to use those. (However, it's part of what makes it so pricey.).

In a recent development, it's been hard to recommend the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft given how expensive it is; it costs as much as ReMarkable's color digital notebook, but that notebook is much more powerful and can double as an e-paper laptop with the keyboard attachment. The Scribe Colorsoft cannot: It's the same as any other Scribe, just with a color screen. But for this price, it's actually worth getting. You'll only pay $50 more than the older model and get a colorful screen to both highlight and draw on.

Looking to escape the Kindle ecosystem, or want your first e-reader to be Amazon-free? The Kobo Libra Colour is both the model and Black Friday deal for you. It features everything that's great about Kindles—a built-in store, compatibility with Libby for library books—plus page-turning buttons and the ability to double as a digital notebook if you buy the Kobo Stylus ($70).

It's only $30 off, and unfortunately this e-reader used to always cost $30 less; Kobo raised its prices earlier this year. But that makes this the best time to buy so that you don't pay the new price and get the previous one. It's also nice that the Kobo Libra Colour includes so many extra features; getting a color screen or page-turn buttons costs much more on a Kindle.

Pocket e-readers are all the rage right now. You might think existing e-readers are small, but the Xteink X4 Pro has just a 4.3-inch screen for reading your books on. It's a fun option to snap onto the back of your phone—it has built-in magnets for this, but a larger phone will be a better fit for that. The X4 Pro adds a touchscreen and home button, making it easier to use than some of Xteink's older models that required more buttons.

Industry observers note that it's easy to send books to the device using the Xteink app, or you can connect it to your computer. It doesn't have any kind of store, so you need to have ePub files of what you want to read on hand, which is a roadblock for some. It's not ideal if you want to read your Libby books, but you can easily send long articles with just the URL through the app to this device, so I love it for reading long essays on a morning commute.

It has been revealed that the base Kindle from 2024 is down to $120 so far for Black Friday, but I recommend waiting to see if it drops down to $104, which is how low it dropped during Prime Day in October. It used to drop to under $100 during deal events, but after Amazon raised its prices this summer, it's more expensive for the same device. The newer versions aren't on sale at all, though, so this older model (which is still great!) is the best to buy if you want something cheaper than the Paperwhite. However, it's not the best deal I've seen for it this fall.

It has been revealed that not every Kindle is on sale. So far, the newest models of the Kindle, Kindle Paperwhite, and Kindle Colorsoft that came out this fall aren't on sale, and neither are the aluminum versions of those newly introduced models. The older Kindle Scribe also isn't on sale. I'm keeping an eye out to see if that changes as Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales continue through the weekend and into early next week.

Industry observers note that taking a refurbished device off the market is a great way to save money — and save that device from going where e-waste goes to die. Refurbished or renewed tablets are often next to impossible to tell apart from a brand new one. Cosmetic dings are a possibility, but unless stated otherwise, the devices have been reworked and tested to run like new. iPads are probably the easiest tablet to find refurbished (at Amazon, Best Buy, and the Apple Store).

Most tablets made specifically for kids will already be equipped with built-in parental accounts, timers, and pre-selected websites or apps that are strictly for kids.

General-purpose tablets aren't a bad choice, either — many sites name the Apple iPad as one of the best tablets for kids even though it's an everyone tablet. These won't have any parental guardrails baked in, so you'll need to get creative if you'd rather your kid not have unlimited access to the internet. Apple and Android have features that can filter or block content and prevent purchases, but the closest thing you'll be able to get to close monitoring is by installing parental control software. Such monitoring features are easy to toggle off or uninstall as your kid gets older or if the family is sharing the device. In the latter case, Osmo is a neat snap-on kit that connects to iPads and Fire tablets for augmented reality-ish learning exercises and games. When your kid moves a physical piece in real life, the same piece moves on the screen. There's always the option of a kids edition tablet too or simply finding the most robust android tablet for younger children.

Apple is a commanding presence in the best tablet field, offering the high-end iPad Pro, the lightweight iPad Air, and the compact iPad mini, but its models come at a premium. They also don't ship with their own accessories (like Apple Pencils or Magic Keyboards), which is an additional cost to consider if you plan on doing a lot of writing or drawing.

In contrast, some Android tablets like the Samsung Galaxy Tab S9 include a stylus pen (the $59.99 Samsung S Pen); there's no additional fee to pay there.

In a recent development, you also need to think about what operating system you prefer. iOS is great to use, but if all your other devices are Android-based, you may prefer to stick with Android. A third option is to consider a ChromeOS-based tablet — but again, you probably want it to play nicely with other devices. Go with what you're comfortable with.

Tablets are a great middle-ground between laptops and smartphones. If you've ever felt like you need more real estate than your smartphone's screen to watch your favorite show, draw a design, or simply browse the internet, a good tablet means you don't have to worry about digging out your laptop. The best tablet blends the convenience of a laptop with the lightweight nature of a phone. Easy to toss into your bag and take traveling, they can entertain your kids or give you something to do while on the move, all without being as full-on as a PC.

If you buy an Apple iPad, you can use FaceTime to call friends and enjoy video chats with them. You can also use iMessage through your iPad with such functionality extending across the range from iPad mini to iPad Pro. However, if you go for an Android tablet, you will need to use a third-party app like WhatsApp, Skype, or Signal to call friends and family.

Dark Matter Might Have Its Own Periodic Table of Invisible Particles

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that dark matter accounts for approximately 85 percent of all matter in the universe, though that’s about all we really know about the mysterious substance.
  • It has been revealed that for decades, scientists have been trying to determine whether dark matter consists of a single type of particle or if it’s made up of several particles that could have different properties and thus different interactions with the surrounding world.
  • This second possibility also raises an intriguing question: If there are a variety of “dark particles,” could they interact and combine with one another—just as the particles we know do—to form their own dark atoms and molecules?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that dark matter accounts for approximately 85 percent of all matter in the universe, though that’s about all we really know about the mysterious substance. Scientists believe it because of the gravitational effects it has on galaxies and other cosmic structures, but since it doesn’t otherwise interact with ordinary matter, it’s been a challenge for scientists to determine what it’s really made of.

It has been revealed that for decades, scientists have been trying to determine whether dark matter consists of a single type of particle or if it’s made up of several particles that could have different properties and thus different interactions with the surrounding world. Earlier this year, scientists found the most convincing evidence of a dark matter particle yet, and if the second scenario is true, it’s possible we could find more.

This second possibility also raises an intriguing question: If there are a variety of “dark particles,” could they interact and combine with one another—just as the particles we know do—to form their own dark atoms and molecules? If that were the case, the dark universe could be much more complex than researchers had initially imagined.

But luckily, humanity has already faced a similar challenge in trying to understand the diversity of ordinary matter. Though to many introductory chemistry students, the periodic table can seem like an odd way to organize information, it’s one of the most ingenious tools developed in our understanding of the physical world. This classification system doesn’t just order the elements, but reveals patterns among their properties that even helped predict the existence of other elements that had not yet been discovered.

In a recent development, now, a team of five physicists is exploring a scenario in which dark matter could form different classes of nuclei and atoms, governed by their own rules. Their research suggests that we may need something similar to a periodic table to understand the organization of dark matter.

Sources indicate that the hypothesis at the heart of this research seems straight out of science fiction. The researchers propose that our universe would contain a kind of “mirror sector,” where particles that barely interact with visible matter have their own forces and can interact with one another.

The idea is not latest and is quite serious. The “Mirror Twin Higgs” was proposed two decades ago as a possible solution to a problem related to the mass of the Higgs boson. According to this theory, mirror particles would help offset certain quantum effects that might otherwise cause its mass to be much greater than what we observe. Although the existence of these particles has never been proven, the proposal offered an ingenious way to address the problem without requiring all new particles to be visible to detectors.

Sources indicate that one of the creators of the Mirror Twin Higgs theory, physicist Zackaria Chacko, is part of this new investigation that extends this hypothesis into the dark matter puzzle. Along with several collaborators, he explores in this recent preprint what would happen if particles from this hypothetical mirror sector could combine with one another, forming nuclei, atoms, and a variety of dark elements.

In a recent development, their calculations suggest that, under certain conditions, these particles could combine to form dark equivalents of some of the elements we know, ranging from the simplest to others as complex as carbon. However, this would not be an exact copy of our matter. The dark particles would have different masses and properties, which would also change the rules governing how they bond, what structures they can form, and which ones remain stable.

In a recent development, for example, in the researchers’ model, dark hydrogen atoms would be unstable and could not survive as those in our universe do. This is a striking difference when we consider that hydrogen is the simplest and most abundant element in ordinary matter.

If these dark elements were ever discovered, understanding the rules governing their formation would be essential for classifying them. A sort of “dark periodic table” could help bring order to that diversity, just as it did with the elements we know.

Sources indicate that for now, this all remains in the realm of theoretical physics. Researchers have not observed any of these atoms, and some doubt such structures could actually form. But there’s plenty about dark matter we have yet to discover.

TL;DR: T-Mobile is offering up to $2,100 off Apple's foldable iPhone Duo via 36 monthly bill credits — with no new line or trade-in required — when you commit seven Picks on a qualifying T-Mix plan.

According to recent reports, we were not expecting to see any meaningful Black Friday discounts on Apple’s first foldable smartphone, but we ended up with a full 100% wipeout. That's the sort of deal that makes Black Friday stop and stand still.

T-Mobile quietly upgraded its Apple iPhone Duo promotion from a $1,200 discount to a full $0 per month offer via 36 monthly bill credits, with no trade-in required. Wow. When you build a qualifying T-Mix blueprint with at least seven Picks, the 256GB iPhone Duo drops from $1,999.99 ($55.56 per month) to absolutely nothing.

At $1,999.99, the iPhone Duo is easily the priciest smartphone in Apple’s lineup. Getting this phone for free without surrendering a current flagship phone or opening an unnecessary extra line is by far the best iPhone deal to drop over Black Friday.

We need to be very clear that while T-Mobile advertises "no new line or trade-in needed," a single-line T-Mix proposal caps out at three Picks (which only knocks $1,200 off, leaving you paying $799.99). Unlocking seven Picks requires a multi-line T-Mix account (specifically, at least three lines starting around $200 per month with AutoPay).

Recent findings suggest that you will also pay upfront sales tax on the full $1,999.99+ retail price plus up to a $35 device connection fee at checkout, stay on your plan for all 36 months to keep the bill credits, and wait out a short backorder (current shipments are estimated for Dec. 9-15). If you're happy to jump through those hoops, the iPhone Duo is yours for $0 per month.

In a recent development, it might be worth the hassle. Mashable's Stan Schroeder used the Duo for a month and remarked: "The advantages of having an iPhone with a massive, beautiful, iPad mini-like display in your pocket simply outweigh all of the compromises that you have to make with the Duo.".
