#3632. Breaking: Swift Saw the Secrets of Space Before Falling to Earth

📅 28 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1100 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Swift Saw the Secrets of Space Before Falling to Earth

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has concluded its scientific mission, which spanned just under 22 years.
  • Sources indicate that swift had been launched on November 20, 2004, as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer, and it began operations the following month.
  • According to recent reports, the development of the Swift space telescope was driven by the difficulty of tracking gamma-ray bursts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has concluded its scientific mission, which spanned just under 22 years. As its orbital altitude fell below 275 kilometers (171 miles), it could no longer continue stable astronomical observations, and it reentered the atmosphere on November 4 over North Sumatra, Indonesia.

Sources indicate that swift had been launched on November 20, 2004, as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer, and it began operations the following month. In addition to a gamma-ray-burst alert telescope, it was equipped with ultraviolet and visible-light telescopes as well as an x-ray telescope, and was designed as a multi-wavelength observation satellite capable of rapidly pinpointing the locations of gamma-ray bursts—the most powerful explosions in the universe. In 2018, following the death of its first principal investigator, Neil Gehrels, NASA renamed the mission in his honor.

According to recent reports, the development of the Swift space telescope was driven by the difficulty of tracking gamma-ray bursts. “Swift was designed as a satellite dedicated to studying gamma-ray bursts, outbursts that came and went so swiftly that no one could target them with large telescopes to learn more,” explains S. Bradley Cenko, the mission’s principal investigator at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.

Sources indicate that swift detected a gamma-ray burst, pinpointed its location, relayed the information to other observatories, and then swiveled its telescope to capture images before the afterglow faded; this sequence of operations was usually finished in about a minute. Speed was particularly critical for short gamma-ray bursts, in which the emissions end in less than two seconds. Before Swift was released, it was not possible to pinpoint the location quickly and accurately enough to observe the afterglow.

Sources indicate that in May 2005, Swift rapidly turned toward the gamma-ray burst GRB 050509B, which lasted only 0.03 second, and detected 11 x-ray photons. This was the first short gamma-ray burst for which an afterglow was detected. This observation corroborated long-standing theoretical models suggesting that short bursts are most likely caused by the merger of two neutron stars, celestial bodies with a mass comparable to the sun compressed to the size of a city.

Its flexible observation planning system is another reason why Swift was regarded as a versatile tool for astronomy. This is because astronomers could request target-of-opportunity observations, which allowed commands to be sent from the ground in as little as a few minutes.

It also allowed for the setup of monitoring programs to observe specific celestial objects for periods ranging from minutes to months, and it was possible to schedule observations of up to 75 distinct celestial objects per day. Furthermore, it played a role in sending alerts to other space- and ground-based facilities to coordinate additional observations.

Industry observers note that swift observed more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and more than 1,400 supernova explosions. It also witnessed stars being torn apart by black holes, monitored active galaxies, and conducted all-sky x-ray surveys; the data from these observations contributed to approximately 7,000 scientific papers. The entire dataset—including approximately 22 years’ worth of brightness measurements and more than 1.5 million images from ultraviolet and visible-light telescopes—is publicly available and amounts to about 12 terabytes.

In a recent development, the Swift observatory was circling in low Earth orbit. At this altitude even the outermost layer of the atmosphere creates air resistance on satellites. However, Swift lacked thrusters to maintain its orbit, and its altitude continued to drop.

It has been revealed that as a result, its altitude—which was approximately 585 kilometers (364 miles) at launch—had dropped to about 363 kilometers as of June 18, 2026. In recent years, increased solar activity has caused Earth’s atmosphere to expand, causing the telescope to descend faster than initially predicted.

In a recent development, NASA engineers had long predicted that Swift’s altitude would drop to approximately 300 kilometers by the fall of 2026, at which point a recovery spacecraft would no longer be able to approach it safely. Consequently, NASA decided not to issue a standard request for proposals and instead asked three companies with which it had already signed technology development contracts to explore the feasibility of providing orbital services. In September 2025, NASA signed a $30 million contract with the space startup Katalyst Space Technologies.

The Swift Space Telescope upon its completion in September 2003. Pictured alongside it is Neil Gehrels, the project’s first principal investigator. (NASA).

The original blueprint was for the small satellite LINK to capture and dock with Swift using three robotic arms, raise its orbit to a safe operational altitude, and resume scientific observations. Since there was only one year to complete this task, Katalyst manufactured components in-house when suppliers could not meet their deadlines and streamlined testing procedures. LINK was launched on July 3, 2026, aboard a Northrop Grumman Pegasus XL rocket.

However, during in-orbit testing, a malfunction occurred in LINK’s attitude-control system, and it was determined that capturing Swift and raising its orbit would be difficult. In response, NASA and Katalyst revealed on August 19 that the operation would be canceled, and the mission was redefined as an in-orbit demonstration.

Industry observers note that LINK raised its orbit to align with Swift, deployed its three robotic arms, and simultaneously fired its three ion thrusters, successfully approaching the telescope to a distance of 12 to 15 kilometers (7 to 9 miles). Nevertheless, NASA unveiled that LINK would not approach Swift any closer during the remainder of its operational life in orbit. LINK subsequently reentered Earth’s atmosphere on September 25.

According to recent reports, following the decision to abandon the orbital raise, the Swift operations team announced a plan to continue observations for as long as possible in the time left. On August 26, they restarted the ultraviolet- and visible-light telescopes and the x-ray telescope—which had been shut down in preparation for the rescue mission—and successfully captured images of Tycho’s supernova remnant, located approximately 13,000 light-years away. But as the altitude dropped below 275 kilometers, the telescope was no longer able to maintain a stable lock on its target, and the scientific mission concluded with the final observation on October 20.

“Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long,” said Sean Domagall-Goldman, director of the Astrophysics Division at NASA headquarters. To ensure it can continue to respond swiftly to cosmic phenomena even after Swift is gone, NASA is considering ways to utilize and expand its existing fleet of space telescopes.

This story was originally published in WIRED Japan and has been translated from Japanese.

It has been revealed that cyber Monday falls on Monday, Nov. 30 this year. While some stores will have a one-day-only sale on that date, most online retailers have evolved into offering a full "Cyber Week" sales event.

Timothy Beck Werth is the Tech Editor at Mashable, where he leads coverage and assignments for the Tech and Shopping verticals. Tim has over 15 years of experience as a journalist and editor, and he has particular experience covering and testing consumer technology, smart home gadgets, and men’s grooming and style products. Previously, he was the Managing Editor and then Site Director of SPY.com, a men's product review and lifestyle website. As a writer for GQ, he covered everything from bull-riding competitions to the best Legos for adults, and he’s also contributed to publications such as The Daily Beast, Gear Patrol, and The Awl.

Tim studied print journalism at the University of Southern California. He at the moment splits his time between Brooklyn, NY and Charleston, SC. He's currently working on his second novel, a science-fiction book.

Sources indicate that this year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27. While retailers often start featuring their best markdowns on Black Friday itself, there are plenty of early deals worth shopping in the lead-up. Most retailers' official sales do start well before the big day, so shopping strategically ahead of time can save you from missing out on a deal entirely (or dealing with the chaos the day after Thanksgiving).

Cyber Monday takes place on the Monday following Thanksgiving. This year, the shopping event falls on Monday, Nov. 30. While Cyber Monday originally began as an online counterpart to in-person shopping on Black Friday, the two events have merged into an extended online shopping bonanza.

Sources indicate that amazon's Black Friday Week sale kicked off on Nov. 19, which means deals have been live for a week now. Amazon has an incentive to spread out the shopping (to give its delivery drivers a break), so you no longer have to wait until actual Black Friday to save. Deals will continue to go live through Nov. 30.

Recent findings suggest that amazon: The retail giant's Black Friday Week sale began on Nov. 19, with new deals dropping daily through Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Recent findings suggest that best Buy: The electronics store's Black Friday sale kicked off on Nov. 19 and runs through Nov. 28. The Best Buy Cyber Monday Sale Event runs for 48 hours on Nov. 29 and Nov. 30.

According to recent reports, walmart: The major box store's Black Friday sale runs from Nov. 23 to Nov. 29 (with deals online only from Nov. 23 to Nov. 26). It's hosting an online-only Cyber Monday sale from Nov. 30 to Dec. 2.

Sources indicate that target: Target's weeklong Black Friday sale started Nov. 22 and goes through Nov. 29.

It has been revealed that the Home Depot: The Home Depot's official Black Friday sale ran from Nov. 5 to Nov. 25, wrapping up before the actual holiday. However, the home improvement store will continue to offer upcoming deals throughout the week, and its Cyber Week sale kicks off on Nov. 30 and runs through Dec. 6.

With the day upon us, in-store Black Friday prices will be live at most retailers on Nov. 27. Openings are as follows:.

Best Buy: 6 a.m. local time, closes at 10 p.m. local time.

Recent findings suggest that home Depot: 6 a.m. local time, closing varies by location.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever come up against a usage limit when sending your Gemini AI assistants off to get a job done, a new capability for Google’s artificial intelligence platform could save you the hassle — and a bunch of time in the process.

Industry observers note that the company has just announced a latest ‘File Slicing Controls’ feature, rolling out across all its models. In a nutshell, it lets you specify which elements of a file you want Gemini to focus on before it gets to work, rather than having the model do a deep scan of an entire file up front, saving you costly usage tokens in the process.

Though it’s primarily aimed at developers, there are elements here anyone can benefit from. The ‘Skim Then Zoom’ workflow is particularly useful — you can, for instance, tell the AI to summarise and explain just the text of a select range of pages in a PDF, and it’ll skim over the other pages and any associated images, just focussing on the passages you request, clawing back time and tokens.

Breaking it down, this might prove one of the most intuitively-useful updates to Gemini in a while:.

For the full run through of how the feature works, check out the Google Blog.

Industry News: 7 Pro Tips to Get More Out of the Google Health App

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if you've been using the Fitbit app in recent years, you'll know that it's now been replaced by Google Health.
  • While many features have been carried over into Google Health from its predecessors, some haven't.
  • Whether you're a veteran from the Google Fit or Fitbit days, or you've just installed Google Health for the first time to use with a fresh device, these tips will help you explore everything the app has to offer and get the most out of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you've been using the Fitbit app in recent years, you'll know that it's now been replaced by Google Health. (Google bought Fitbit back in 2019.) The app will eventually replace Google Fit too, though we don't know exactly when that will be. Google has previously said it will happen before the end of the year.

While many features have been carried over into Google Health from its predecessors, some haven't. There have also been new additions, and a lot of rearranging has gone on too, so it can take a while to figure out exactly where everything is.

Whether you're a veteran from the Google Fit or Fitbit days, or you've just installed Google Health for the first time to use with a fresh device, these tips will help you explore everything the app has to offer and get the most out of it.

Industry observers note that if you've been waiting to buy a device to track your steps before installing Google Health, you don't have to. You can still get the step-tracking features from the app, as long as you carry your phone with you on all your walks and runs.

In a recent development, tap the Connections icon (top left), then Phone to start pulling in data from your Android or iOS smartphone. If you later add a wearable, you can switch to this for steps—or keep them both enabled (handy if you forget your tracker at home one day, for example).

The Today page is the first one you see when you open the Google Health app, so it makes sense to fill it with the stats that actually matter to you, rather than the metrics the app picks. Tap the pen icon just underneath the top bank of widgets to make changes.

You're able to switch between Standard view and Expanded view, depending on how much health and fitness information you want to see at once. In both views, you can swipe right or left to see more widgets.

According to recent reports, tap the + (plus) icon next to any widget you want to add to the Today page, and the - (minus) icon next to any widget you want to remove. Hiding widgets doesn't do anything to your fitness data, it just means that data isn't shown on the Today view.

It has been revealed that you don't have to rely on your fitness tracker, smartwatch, or phone to capture all of your movement. To add something manually, tap Log on the Today view, then Activity, and pick the activity type—like Walk, Basketball, Indoor climbing, or whatever it is.

Recent findings suggest that the app asks you to fill out key details, like the start and end points of the activity, before saving the record. You can manually add lots of other information from the same screens, from the hours you’ve slept to the meals you've had.

There are various parts of the Google Health interface, including the widgets on the Today page, where you'll see references to your health and fitness goals. These aren't going to be all that useful to you if you just leave the default values in place.

Recent findings suggest that to make these metrics more meaningful, tap your profile picture (top right), then choose Google Health settings > Activity. You'll find numerous goals listed here, together with a few other settings, like whether or not to detect activities automatically.

Sources indicate that tap on any goal to set it or edit it. These targets affect the layout of screens throughout the app, and you might get notifications about them too, from time to time—if you don't want this, choose Manage notifications from the Activity screen.

You'll of course want your fitness tracker or smartwatch to be logging everything as accurately as possible. Even if the step counts are only off by a little each day, that can add up to a significant difference over the weeks and months.

Industry observers note that there are two settings to check here: If you tap your profile picture (top right), then choose Google Health settings > Activity, you can set your Stride length. This lets you give Google Health more precise measurements for your gait, whether walking or running.

Recent findings suggest that second, tap the Connections icon (top left), then your wearable. Choose Device preferences, and you can tell the app which wrist your wearable is usually on, which should mean more accurate step and movement tracking.

According to recent reports, you may have seen mentions of Google Health Premium in the app or seen pop-ups about it, but what exactly is it? And what do you get for your money? The subscription replaces the old Fitbit Premium and works along similar lines.

It has been revealed that for $10 a month, you get personalized and adaptable health intends that give you specific instructions for reaching your health and fitness goals. You also get a Gemini-powered AI Coach that gives you workout recaps and fitness advice based on the metrics you're recording.

The sleep summaries are more detailed in terms of sleep stages and the sleep scoring system. You also get access to a library of guided workouts and mindfulness sessions in the app.

One extra note: If you're signed up for one of Google's AI plans at the $20-per-month tier or higher, you get Google Health Premium thrown in as part of it (as well as Google Home Premium and YouTube Premium Lite).

It's possible that you want all the Google Health Premium extras but find the AI Coach a bit intrusive. It does take a very proactive stance when it comes to giving you tips and pointers, but it can be a bit too eager to help.

To hide it from view, tap your profile picture (top right), then Google Health settings > Coach. From here you can opt out of the Coach feature entirely or just hide the main insights from view. (You'll still be able to ask questions about your data.) When you need the coach’s encouragement and you want to turn it back on, you can do so in the same place.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that samsung might be gearing up for another massive change to its flagship phone cameras.
  • In a recent development, the claim comes from well-known leaker Ice Universe, who shared the alleged changes on X.
  • For the uninitiated, the laser autofocus module is supposed to emit an infrared beam and calculate the time it takes to bounce back from a subject, then use the distance information to assist the camera in locking focus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that samsung might be gearing up for another massive change to its flagship phone cameras. A newly introduced leak suggests Samsung is likely to ditch the laser autofocus hardware, possibly taking the 3x telephoto camera with it. That’s two changes to the rear camera system, and while neither is necessarily a recipe for photographic trouble, it does bring up an interesting question: what does Samsung intend to use instead?

In a recent development, the claim comes from well-known leaker Ice Universe, who shared the alleged changes on X. Samsung has been using laser autofocus in its Ultra phones since the Galaxy S21 Ultra, so this is a departure from a camera setup the company has used for several generations.

For the uninitiated, the laser autofocus module is supposed to emit an infrared beam and calculate the time it takes to bounce back from a subject, then use the distance information to assist the camera in locking focus.

This is particularly helpful in low-light situations, where traditional phase-detection autofocus (PDAF) can struggle. But laser autofocus has its own limitations. It struggles with distant subjects, bright sunlight and moving objects.

That doesn't necessarily mean the S27 Ultra will have a worse camera. Autofocus technology has come a long way. Both dual-pixel and all-pixel autofocus can calculate the distance to a subject by using multiple light-sensitive areas across the image sensor. This technology is already being used in some of Samsung’s other flagship devices, so the ditching of a separate laser module is not necessarily a step backward.

It’s also rumored that Samsung might utilize its newly introduced 200MP ISOCELL HP6 sensor for the Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro. Previous reports have indicated support for LOFIC, a technology that’s designed to improve HDR photography and preserve detail in the brightest and darkest parts of a photo. It’s not known if the new sensor will also introduce an advanced autofocus system as well.

In a recent development, the bigger question is what these hardware changes portend for everyday photography. The lack of a dedicated 3x camera may mean more reliance on cropping the sensor for zoom ranges in between. The removal of laser autofocus may mean more reliance on the main sensor’s focusing system.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Industry observers note that none of these changes have been confirmed by Samsung, and we won’t see the Galaxy S27 family until the first quarter of 2027. Whether these rumored changes are a smart play for newer imaging tech or just another instance of stripping out useful hardware to cut costs is something buyers will want answered before splashing out flagship money.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials.
  • The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” ….
  • Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler claims that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials. The database was neither password-protected nor encrypted.

The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” ….

Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler claims that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.

I also observed thousands of Tor .onion addresses associated with account names and passwords. The Tor .onion services are generally categorized as part of the dark web, and these credentials could potentially provide access to private forums, marketplaces, communication platforms, or other hidden services. While .onion accounts alone do not imply criminal or malicious activity, it is estimated that as much as 60% of dark web sites host illegal material and illicit activities. This is the first time I have seen a large number of dark web accounts in breached credentials. It should be noted that legitimate organizations, journalists, whistleblower platforms, and news organizations also operate .onion services to provide anonymity and bypass censorship.

But the most frightening aspect of it is separate folders for individual victims containing all of the information needed for identity theft.

Fowler told Wired that this data appears to have been obtained through advanced malware.

Sources indicate that the “scariest” thing in the database, Fowler indicates, was around 400,000 documents that appeared to come from “more advanced malware” compiling information about individual victims […] that create a detailed profile of an individual and their digital life. “If you had that, you own that person,” Fowler says.

According to recent reports, there’s no information about the specific sources of the data, but it seems likely to be aggregated from a range of data breaches. Fowler contacted the hosting company to have the database removed, but it’s not known how many people may have had access to it.

According to recent reports, the best protection is to use a password manager like Apple’s Passwords app to ensure you have strong, unique passwords for each individual website and service you use, with two-factor authentication enabled wherever possible. When given the choice of 2FA code delivery, you should always opt for an authenticator app rather than a text message to protect yourself against SIM-swap attacks.

This is the lowest price on Amazon; however, it has dropped to this price before. Note that Walmart and Best Buy are also offering the XM6 at this sale price.

Good gaming laptops are never cheap, and they’ve become even more expensive this year. Industry observers note that the Pixel 11-series phones from Google are among our favorite Android devices. Breaking: TIME’s Top 100 Photos of 2026 list includes a shot taken on iPhone 18 Pro

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In September, Apple held a photography exhibition in New York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera.
  • TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year.
  • Recent findings suggest that the essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In September, Apple held a photography exhibition in New York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos.

TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year. The list showcases the pictures that the TIME Photo Department determines best capture that particular year.

Recent findings suggest that the essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism. Someone was there. A news photographer lifted a viewfinder, pressed a button, and captured an instant happening in front of them.

Chin’s image was shot in Bugaboo Provincial Park, Canada, on iPhone 18 Pro. He explained that a traditional production creates a layer of separation between the photographer and the subject, with equipment, crew, and all the moving parts of a shoot. Shooting on iPhone 18 Pro meant that he could create a more intimate environment, allowing for a sense of comfort and spontaneity that comes through in the images.

Image Courtesy of Apple (as featured in the What Holds Us exhibition).

Chin’s goal was to capture the intersection of human ambition and the pursuit of wonder against the backdrop of a timeless natural landscape.

“The resolution and the sharpness on iPhone 18 Pro surprised me. I could shoot a few inches of rock and ice, or a massive panorama, and trust it would hold at size. That is what this work needed. It also meant I carried almost nothing. In the mountains, everything you carry is a decision. I was not thinking about gear. I was thinking about what was in front of me.”.

Apple’s “What Holds Us” exhibit ran in Upcoming York City in September, featuring work from photographers Alex Prager, Jack Davison, and Jimmy Chin, with each artist using the iPhone 18 Pro to explore the “people, places, and ideas that connect and ground humanity.” Kathy Ryan, the former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, curated the exhibition.

Industry observers note that the exhibit is now headed to London, where it will open to the public on December 4, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It will also be open from Saturday, December 12 through Sunday, December 13, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

You can view the full list of this year’s TIME 100 Photos right here.

According to recent reports, I have to be honest here: most streaming deals aren't going to turn your finances around in any life-changing way. The Black Friday streaming price cuts have become steadily less tempting over the past few years. They're just not as impressive as they used to be. It's also worth noting that most deals apply only to the ad-supported tiers (with just a few exceptions). Still, any and every discount is welcome in a time when prices keep rising. Every cent counts, and it's easy to lose track of just how much you spend on streaming — especially if you're signed up for more than one service.

Most streamers announced their Black Friday deals early this week, but you may be wondering if there are still more to come. With just a couple of days until Cyber Monday, I'd say the best streaming deals have already arrived. I can't imagine that many more will pop up at this stage.

I'm shocked that Peacock's Black Friday deal is as good as it is for 2026. Last year, the streamer didn't offer a deal at all, so this is light-years better than I was expecting. If you've been holding off on subscribing, now is likely the only time you'll get a decent discount. The Paramount+, HBO Max, and Disney+/Hulu Black Friday offers are pretty much on par with their deals of years past. I would lock in HBO Max and the Disney+/Hulu bundle for a full year, as more price increases could pop up in 2027. Paramount+ tends to offer discounts throughout the year more than any other streamer, so if you miss out on this one, it's no biggie.

It has been revealed that it's not worth holding on for a Netflix Black Friday deal, unfortunately. Netflix has never offered a Black Friday discount, or any kind of discount for that matter. Netflix is the top name in streaming and apparently feels that it doesn't need to offer Black Friday deals. I don't expect this year to be any different, but I'm always willing to be proven wrong. It would be a nice and welcome surprise.

We'll be updating this list of the best Black Friday streaming deals on the off chance any more turn up, so be sure to check back for updates.

Industry observers note that in case you missed it, the Thanksgiving Day parade was postponed for the first time in history due to weather. Instead of airing live on Thanksgiving Day as usual, it will air on Saturday, Nov. 28 at 8:30 a.m. You can stream the parade live on Peacock on Saturday or watch last year's parade on Thanksgiving Day. The Peacock Select tier will not grant you access; you'll need a Premium subscription.

Unfortunately, Netflix is one of the only streamers that just straight up does not participate in Black Friday. We've never seen a discounted subscription in years past and don't expect one in 2026. Of course, we're happy to be proven wrong.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CAD images of the iPhone 18e, stated to come from a previously reliable source, have shown a rather odd new design for the camera bump.

If accurate, it would represent a big change from its predecessor, which simply has a single lens protruding without a surrounding bump or plateau ….

In a recent development, the iPhone 17e was rolled out in March with a design unchanged from last year’s iPhone 16e. While the camera did get some feature enhancements, including the ability to store depth information for portrait photos, the physical camera design remained the same.

The current model has a single lens protruding directly from the casing with a flush-mounted flashlight next to it. Engadget reports on CAD images showing a very different approach with next year’s iPhone 18e.

The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone.

The site doesn’t share the images, but claims that the camera bump looks similar to that of the M5 iPad Pro, shown below.

It’s unclear what might have prompted the change of design, especially as the site’s Filipe Espósito says he’s also seen CAD models for the standard model iPhone 18 or the iPhone Air 2, neither of which adopt it.

Previous reports have suggested that the only spec change with the iPhone 18e over its predecessor will be performance improvements thanks to the A20 chip.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alongside a teaser for the newly introduced Ear (note) recorder, Nothing CEO Carl Pei has confirmed the organization’s intends for a big 2027 in terms of smartphone releases, as well as a focus on the US market.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Carl Pei says that Nothing currently has “tens of millions of devices in use,” and that there are massive looks for 2027.

This includes “more attention” to the US market for Nothing, with the US being Nothing’s fastest-growing market for audio devices. In 2026, Nothing launched its Ear (3a) earbuds, multiple CMF-branded devices, and two pairs of over-ear headphones including its high-end Headphone (1) Pro in September, all of which are sold in the US (and on sale during Black Friday).

It has been revealed that pei further stated that Nothing would have a more “aggressive” smartphone release schedule in 2027. Previously, it was said that Nothing would launch six latest smartphones next year, following just three new smartphones in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that pei mentioned Nothing now has “tens of millions of devices in use” across its smartphones, earbuds and other products. The tech giant is also planning to devote more attention to the US market, while pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next year than it did in 2026.

The tech giant said it has generated more than $2 billion in revenue since its first product release in 2022 and that the US is its fastest growing market for audio gear.

Industry observers note that nothing doesn’t have a strict schedule for fresh product debuts, but Nothing Phone (4a) debuted in March 2026, with Phone (3) launching in the Summer of the year prior. With six new devices supposedly in the works, it’s anyone’s guess as to when they might release.

  • Recent findings suggest that 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off.
  • Industry observers note that with iPhone Handoff, you can use the same phone number on two different iPhones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iPhone Handoff is a new feature in iOS 27 that lets you use the same phone number across two different iPhones. However, the feature requires carrier support, so it isn’t available to everyone. Here are the carriers that at the moment support iPhone Handoff and those that have promised support.

Recent findings suggest that 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

Industry observers note that with iPhone Handoff, you can use the same phone number on two different iPhones. Your number automatically moves between the two phones, depending on which one you pick up. This includes calls, voicemail, messages, and Find My location.

According to recent reports, simply unlock whichever device you want to use and you’re ready to go. Other data synced with iCloud will automatically update across your devices. Third-party apps work across both devices, following each app’s own syncing behavior.

iPhone Handoff is available on iOS 27 and later. The phones must be connected to Wi-Fi, share the same Apple Account, use Messages in iCloud, and be signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account.

Industry observers note that the biggest limiting factor of iPhone Handoff is that it requires carrier support. Right now, just three carriers support the feature:.

What about carriers that are working on the feature? In the United States, Verizon has promised it “will support iPhone Handoff,” but it’s unclear when the feature will launch. Verizon states it will charge $10 per month for the service.

According to recent reports, AT&T, meanwhile, has no intends to support iPhone Handoff. In a statement in September, the carrier stated that its focus “remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” The carrier noted that there “could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” but that customers should use “existing eSIM activation and transfer options” instead.

No other carriers have promised support for iPhone Handoff, so it’s unclear how promptly the feature will expand around the world.

Industry observers note that in my testing, iPhone Handoff works really well. I have it set up between my iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. I use the iPhone Duo 90% of the time, but when I do pick up my iPhone 18 Pro, my number instantly switches to it. There’s a cute animation that expands from the Dynamic Island, confirming that the number has moved.

In a recent development, have you tried iPhone Handoff? Are you willing to pay extra for it? Let us know down in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that good morning. Today I’m deciding whether the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer passes the “people just standing around” test, trying the latest Material 3 Expressive Claude app on my Android devices, and stocking up on discounted XTEINK e-readers for Christmas gifts.

According to recent reports, inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that eleven days after leaving Nvidia, Jensen Huang is back as president, CEO, and a board director. The board voted unanimously to reinstate him on Monday, saying it was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead following a series of meetings. It also said input from senior levels of the US government left it confident that his reinstatement poses no national security risk.

According to recent reports, I didn’t see this coming. Huang was dishonest to the public and to his board. He admitted to having affairs not only with an alleged Chinese spy, but also with an employee who directly reported to him. He is accused of facilitating the sale of Nvidia AI chips to companies like Megaspeed that knowingly purchased them with the intention of smuggling them into China, a contravention of US trade restrictions.

As recently as November 17th, the board chair, Harvey Jones, reiterated that the organization had no intention of bringing back Huang as CEO. But things changed quickly on Sunday as President Trump reportedly reassured the board that Huang’s reinstatement posed no security risk to US intelligence, something that the new Democratic-led Congress will be sure to test via repeated subpoenas in the new year.

As Huang walked into the atrium at Nvidia’s headquarters, staff gathered around to cheer his return, and he addressed the crowd by saying he would be a “better CEO the second time around,” as if 11 days of unemployment had given him sufficient time to evaluate his past behavior.

Nvidia’s stock was up over 30% on Monday, rebounding from a disastrous end to last week that wiped out $4 trillion in Nasdaq value. It’s hard not to see Huang’s return as a direct response to this short-term disruption, which also hinted at a much more serious correction in the stock market. Nvidia’s stock had already fallen 24% between the day Huang resigned and Friday’s crunch, and with looming regulation from Congress in 2027, a rudderless AI industry could have been disastrous for the US economy writ large.

It has been revealed that though things may appear to be back to normal, or as normal as possible given the insanity of the past couple of weeks, Huang has returned to a very different trade environment. While he was away, Nvidia’s board formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to investigate whether the company’s actions violated any US embargoes. And as part of Huang’s return, Nvidia has committed to hiring its first chief compliance officer, an executive who will ostensibly not report directly to the CEO.

I was pretty gobsmacked when I saw the news of Huang’s return come across the wire at 9am ET yesterday. I’m still wrapping my head around it. Is Nvidia too substantial to fail, or just a symptom of a larger interdependency between the US executive branch and Big Tech? Huang promises to be a better leader this time around, but to whom: his employees, his customers, or his shareholders? Because he appears to be a very different person to each of those groups.

And because the Watch 9 is basically identical, I’d go for the Watch 8. A deal on the year’s best Android foldable: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is showing up at $1,499.99 for some lucky shoppers and $1,549.99 for the rest. Either way, it’s Samsung’s best product of 2026, and my current favorite gadget.

Google’s latest mid-sized sedan AI model is taking the world by storm. Gemini 4 Neon is technically the middle sibling in Google’s lineup, with Carbon at the top and Hydrogen at the bottom, but everyone seems to agree it absolutely cooks.

Sources indicate that if you’ve spent any time on X over the past few days (I hate myself for writing that), you’ll likely have seen an uptick in fervor over Google’s latest model, which seems to outperform Claude Opus 5.5, and even Gemini 4 Carbon itself, in many benchmarks and real-world tests. Even Google is providing some helpful guidance about when to use one or the other.

According to recent reports, one thing I’ve read again and again about Neon is how adept it is at writing. I’m of two minds about this: the better an AI gets at doing my job, the less necessary I am at noted job. On the other hand, I’m so tired of obvious AI slop that a model that actually writes well sounds like a relief. At least when I’m unemployed, I won’t be yelling at the screen all day about why the robot yet again used negative parallelism.

It has been revealed that I didn’t get to play much GTA VI over the weekend, but I know a few (million) people who did. Publisher Take-Two indicates the game generated $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales. That’s an incredible number in any industry, but a truly mind-blowing one in the video game world. Rockstar also released its first patch for the game on Monday to fix a modest number of bugs with the launch code.

If you follow open-weight AI models, you’ll likely have heard of how influential Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 was when it launched in June. Now the manufacturer has released GLM-5.4, and it’s novel as much for its architecture as it is for its benchmarks.

In a recent development, its Loop Transformer reuses a block of layers to do more computation without adding parameters. The firm is pitching applications beyond software, including games, visual work, and CAD. The 750-million-parameter model reportedly performs at the level of a 2-3 trillion parameter non-looping equivalent, but we’re still waiting on a broader release for real-world testing.

According to recent reports, in browser news, Ladybird’s first public alpha is now downloadable for macOS and Linux. It’s built with a brand-new engine that eschews many of the legacy decisions made by Google’s Chromium team. And the project has the backing of big names like Shopify, Cloudflare, and Proton. It’s still pretty rough, and features are paltry, but any new competition in the browser space is a win in my book.

The debate over the wisdom and safety of using Meta’s Muse AI agent continues as the app rolls out in the UK. It follows a warning by a number of regulatory bodies about the potential risks of AI agents ….

Meta yesterday announced the UK availability of Muse.

Muse, Meta’s personal Al agent, is now available to adults in the UK. Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar. To get those jobs done you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the retailer apps you shop on.

According to recent reports, A forum representing four different UK regulatory bodies last month issued a warning about the potential dangers involved in using AI agents. The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum remarked:.

Industry observers note that AI agents may amplify and accelerate risks and introduce latest ones. These risks may increase as the capabilities of personal agents grow and adoption rises. Questions of consumer protection, competition and data protection – for example the risk of fraud and scams, personal information sharing not in line with user expectations and misleading recommendations, decisions or information provided – must be addressed to ensure innovation develops in ways that earn and maintain public trust.

Meta has pushed back against suggestions that Muse has accessed personal data without permission, insisting that users are in control and must approve crucial actions. The company has admitted to some “isolated incidents,” but states other reported breaches were either hallucinations or took place on internal versions of the app while undergoing testing. In a newly introduced blog post, Meta says:.

In a recent development, muse only works with the apps and services you choose to connect it to, and you control the access it gets […] Once you’ve decided what Muse is connected to and what you want it to do, with your oversight, it can handle tasks like searching, comparing and planning for you. But before it does anything like sending an email or buying something, it highlights you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your go-ahead. A separate security agent checks Muse’s actions and the information it sends out against the permissions you’ve granted. You can also choose how often it checks in with you in Settings.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, Muse remains the second most popular free app in Apple’s US App Store, with more than 10 million downloads. We reported yesterday that some banks are already blocking AI agents, while others are warning that they will not be responsible for the consequences of any actions taken by them.

Okay, so here’s the deal (literally): last year’s Moto G Stylus (2025) is on sale right now on Amazon for just $199, and if you desperately need a digital writing tool with your phone, it’s a good buy.

That is the short answer; the long answer is a little more complicated, as due to some issues with the 2026 model, you are missing out on exactly…nothing. Yes, at under $200, you are getting essentially the same phone because Motorola decided that, due to RAM and storage shortages and price hikes, the newer model would forgo any major upgrades. The 2026 model starts at $499, so if you had your eye on it, yeah, it’s a silly way to waste $300 in our opinion.

Industry observers note that it has the same Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 processor, 8GB RAM, and 128GB storage. There’s a 120Hz display too and the good news is you get a microSD card slot to expand the storage if you desperately need it. Other notable features include a 5,000mAh battery, 68W wired charging, 15W wireless charging, a 50MP camera setup, and, as of writing, it should be due for an Android 16 upgrade.

The star of the show of the Moto G Stylus (2025) is the stylus. It boils down to this: if you want a phone that isn’t a Galaxy Ultra, then this is the only other line that makes sense for document signers.

However, there are better deals out there. I think the Galaxy A56, at just $299, is an incredible offer right now and way more deserving of your hard-earned cash. Even so, if you want clean software or that stylus, the Moto G Stylus (2025) at $199 is at least an option especially for a family member or a backup to your existing phone.

iOS 27 brought several newly introduced features to the Messages app, including a setting that’s long been a popular request: the ability to customize or turn off the audio button. Here’s how to use it.

Sources indicate that siri AI is the biggest example of that, offering a massive upgrade over the old Siri. But smaller changes in apps like Calendar, Mail, and Messages reflect this focus on wish fulfillment.

In a recent development, in Messages, there’s a upcoming setting that I instantly starting using. It lets you turn off the audio button that normally lives on the right side of the text input field.

According to recent reports, the audio button has been conveniently accessible there for years, but I never use it. I don’t think I’ve ever sent an audio message. Sometimes I use dictation, but that’s always available from the bottom-right of the keyboard.

According to recent reports, since I never need that button, the only time it gets pressed is by accident. And as I suspect a lot of users have encountered—including Justin Bieber—it’s very easy to hit by accident.

Industry observers note that thankfully, iOS 27 has the fix. To disable the audio button, follow these steps:.

Even if you turn the audio button off, you can still send audio messages by hitting the + button to open your iMessage apps then selecting ‘Audio.’.

If you prefer to keep the button active, you can alternately now select ‘Record Audio’ or ‘Start Dictation’ as its function. That way the button will always stay set to your preference instead of dynamically changing like it did before.

Will you disable the audio button in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frontier AI models that have yet to be released by OpenAI and Anthropic are reportedly reaching the point where employees believe they cannot be safely released or controlled, employees reportedly say.

Axios cites “more than two dozen” employees inside of OpenAI and Anthropic who are sounding warnings around unreleased models from both companies.

In a recent development, while both OpenAI’s GPT and Anthropic’s Claude public models are increasingly powerful, these employees say that fresh models behind the scenes are starting to beat out the technical solutions for controlling them. This has led to debates between those who think they’ll be able to fix these problems, and others who believe companies should stop training new models altogether due to the risks.

It has been revealed that if we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us … they will in fact be able to trick us successfully. And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.

The report goes out to point out that some researchers feel that executives at major AI companies have become “out of touch” with the severity of safety risks, though Axios was told that OpenAI is adopting new safety practices while Anthropic mentioned that “Keeping a model internal doesn’t make it safe,” adding that “we may slow down or hold back even when it costs us.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following its debut on the Galaxy Watch 9 earlier this year, Samsung is finally rolling out Wear OS 7 to older Galaxy Watch models with its One UI 9 Watch enhancement.

Samsung’s One UI 9 Watch update is largely focused on newly introduced health features including Vitals, Heart Health Score, Daily Cardio Load, Fitness Index, and improvements to both Sleep Coaching and Sleep Apnea alerts.

“Vitals” is perhaps the most useful day-to-day addition, with Samsung Health collecting data on key vital signs such as heart rate, heart rate variability, respiratory rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen and establishing a range so you can see when your vitals are out of the usual range.

One UI 9 Watch is based on Wear OS 7, and also includes an improved Compass app with “Track Back,” a feature that helps people to follow their route back to a recorded point.

There’s also a latest “Portrait Watch Face” that can adjust the clock face around the subject of a photo.

Samsung is, as of today, officially rolling out One UI 9 Watch with Wear OS 7 to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Galaxy Watch 8 Classic. Meanwhile, the enhancement is in beta for several other older models which will be updated soon including:.

The Galaxy Watch 5 series and Watch FE should also be getting the update, but no beta is available for those devices. Samsung’s first Wear OS watches, the Galaxy Watch 4 series, will not get the update.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ready or not, the holiday shopping season is underway. Choosing the best Christmas gifts for the ones you love is either an epic quest that you look forward to every year — or one you dread. Luckily, we spend our days testing all the latest gadgets, trending products, and gift-worthy gear, and we know exactly what to recommend.

Even better, now that retailers like Best Buy and Amazon have introduced their official Black Friday sales, you can buy about half of our favorite gifts on sale right now.

According to recent reports, for 2026, our Christmas wishlist is simple: it's all the awesome stuff we loved most this year, including the products we named Mashable Gift of the Year winners. That includes the newest gadgets, the swoonworthy items we just had to buy for ourselves, and some classic all-time Mashable favorites. With input from our own tech reporters, shopping editors, and product reviewers, every single Christmas gift idea we recommend is an item we use, love, or have given to others ourselves.

Whether you're searching for the best Christmas gifts for mom and dad, your sweetheart, cool teens, or stocking stuffers everyone will love, start with our Christmas gift guide. So, join us as we put on our Santa hats and share the very best Christmas gift ideas of the year.

Several Mashable reporters dramatically curbed their screen time with the help of the Brick, a pocket-sized gadget that locks certain apps on your phone. That physical element makes it way more effective than traditional screen-time apps. "My favorite use of Bricking my phone is before bed, as it ensures social media isn't the first thing I see when I wake up," said lead shopping reporter Samantha Mangino. Throw in a cute Brick Case while you're at it, too. Read our full review of the Brick.

Charging devices are always some of the best practical gifts and stocking stuffers. Anker has an endless number of high-powered charging solutions, but we’re especially fond of two. First, the ultra-thin Nano MagSafe Power Bank attaches magnetically to compatible phones for convenient wireless charging. Then, there’s the Nano Smart Display Charger, which can fast-charge smartphones and let you know when it's done with a built-in smart display.

It has been revealed that wired earbuds are back in style, and Apple's EarPods — the white 'buds that used to come with old iPhones — are a classic, affordable option. Senior shopping reporter Haley Henschel replaced her uncomfortable AirPods Pro 2 with them and never looked back. "Join me on the wired side," she wrote. "The sound quality is good enough [and] the cover charge is cheap.".

The Kodak Charmera is a miniature camera that comes in a blind box (like a Labubu), so you don't know exactly which color you're going to get. The best part is that it can actually take photos and videos — it's not just a decorative toy — and its shots are delightfully nostalgic. Multiple Mashable staffers have one of these hanging on their keychains or purses' hardware.

It has been revealed that the Nothing Ear (3a) are an excellent AirPods Pro alternative and some of the best budget earbuds available. They sound as good as they look, delivering clear, bold audio in a transparent design. Call quality is their biggest strength, rivaling earbuds that cost nearly three times as much.

Industry observers note that these rechargeable electric hand warmers come personally recommended by Mashable tech editor Timothy Beck Werth, who's been slipping them into Christmas stockings for years. They have a cute design and built-in flashlight, but most importantly, they keep your hands and fingers nice and toasty even in the bitter cold. If you're looking for gifts under $25 for a White Elephant or Secret Santa gift exchange, we promise these will be popular.

A Welly first-aid kit is another of our go-to stocking stuffers. The brand is best known for its adorable, kid-friendly Bravery Bandages with fun designs, but even adults will appreciate this colorful and travel-friendly med kit, which has all the essentials you need to treat little bumps, scrapes, burns, and ouchies. Pack one in your dopp kit when you travel, or keep it in your medicine cabinet year-round.

Amazon just dropped some iPad alternatives for Android consumers with tighter budgets: the upcoming Alexa tablets. Their premium aluminum chassis are sleek and colorful, and the Alexa+ AI assistant is built right into them. Plus, unlike Amazon's older Fire tablets, they have full access to the Google Play Store. If your gifting budget has no bounds, we think the high-end Alexa Tablet 12 Pro with an optional "nanomatte" display is one of the best Christmas gift ideas for digital artists.

In a recent development, the Ambient Dreamie is a fresh smart alarm clock that "makes it easy to pretend like your phone doesn't exist," Henschel wrote. "It doesn't require an app for setup, and it eliminates most excuses for bringing your phone to bed by offloading your alarms, night lighting, and sleep content." She said it helped her fall asleep faster and wake up easier. This fall, the Dreamie added a podcast feature, and contactless sleep tracking is next on the docket. Read our full review of the Ambient Dreamie.

Apple finally revisited its HomePod mini smart speaker this fall to give it a faster processor and a newly introduced "Sound Glow" feature that can sync with your music. A future software upgrade will add support for the company's Siri AI assistant; if you link it to your phone or iPad, it'll be able to recognize your voice and complete tasks for you using your calendar, texts, and emails. Crucially, it also now comes in pink and green.

In a recent development, this spring, Apple dropped a budget bombshell in the MacBook Neo, a colorful laptop that doesn't look or feel as cheap as it really is. (It starts at just $699.) "Most cheap Windows laptops and Chromebooks have plastic components, but this little guy has the same luxe, all-aluminum build quality as any other MacBook," Henschel wrote, adding that its A18 Pro chip is "extremely impressive" in basic computing scenarios. It's a Mashable Choice Award winner, and we think it's the best laptop for kids and younger students. Read our full review of the Apple MacBook Neo.

According to recent reports, shopping for someone who runs every decision past ChatGPT? We've got just the thing. We’re talking about Pocket, a voice recorder that hides discreetly in any pocket. Moreover, this is a personal AI assistant programmed to take notes, transcribe meetings, and summarize calls. Pocket does a terrific job of extracting key info and providing visual maps of conversations. It's also a great gift idea for college students.

Another Mashable Choice titleholder, the latest Oura Ring 5 has a slimmer design that makes it more comfortable to wear for long periods of time — yet it still lasts up to seven days per charge. According to Mangino, who's used to wearing an Apple Watch, its jewelry-like look and fit make it the ultimate everyday wearable. Its "exceptional" activity tracking (her words) and useful health insights are just the icing on the cake. Read our full review of the Oura Ring 5.

Industry observers note that pokémon fever is running high for the legendary franchise's 30th anniversary. So, whether you're shopping for a 5-year-old or a nostalgic millennial who’s still a kid at heart, expect Pokémon gifts to be in very high demand for Christmas 2026.

Select brands have collaborated with the IP to release various special-edition products, including Adidas and Beats. We're also huge fans of the adorable Lego Smart Play Pokémon sets. Our advice: grab available items ASAP or bookmark product pages to watch for restocks. You can thank us later.

According to recent reports, A fitting gift for any modern bookworm is an e-reader. We've also named the upcoming Amazon Kindles some of our favorite Christmas gift ideas of the year (keep scrolling), but there are other options we love. Another Mashable favorite, the Kobo Libra Colour, lets readers highlight passages in color and makes comic books and graphic novels more engaging. We also love the new reMarkable Paper Pure, a powerhouse e-ink writing tablet that doubles as an e-reader for PDF and ePub files, without any ads or pop-ups. Read more about the best e-readers.

We think the TCL QM6K is the best TV for most people. Former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart deemed it "the quintessential beginner fancy TV": a nice QLED model with adequate brightness, deep blacks, great color, and a high-enough refresh rate for gaming, but a reasonable price tag. (Every size is usually on sale for well under $1,000 — even the huge 85-incher.) It's primo "for casual home theater purposes," Stodart wrote. Read our full review of the TCL QM6K.

In a recent development, there are plenty of ways to trick out a new iPhone. Moft’s cult-favorite, origami-styled phone stand is a great tech stocking stuffer that magnetically snaps onto the back of a phone and folds into three viewing positions. A built-in sleeve holds up to two cards, giving you some on-the-go and on-the-desk swagger. It's compatible with all MagSafe iPhones (and Android devices with magnets), making it one of the best Christmas gifts under $50.

Recent findings suggest that birdbuddy's smart feeders are super popular Christmas gifts, and the brand just came out with two fresh models: the Birdbuddy Nook and Birdbuddy Home. Henschel tested them and prefers the Home because it has a larger seed reservoir and two built-in solar panels. However, the small, affordable Nook is "ideal for tight spaces like balconies and patios," she said. Both feeders are super easy to set up and have an upgraded, scratch-resistant camera with AI-powered bird species recognition.

Sources indicate that this fall, Apple came out with its first-ever smart display, the HomeView. Parents can use it for FaceTime calls, sending messages, listening to music, catching up on demonstrates, and answering questions or controlling other smart home devices via Siri AI. It also doubles as a digital picture frame. (Like Amazon's Echo Show devices, it's basically an all-in-one hub.) Up to six people can set up their own profiles on it, so it's well-suited for bigger households. Read our first impressions of the Apple HomeView.

Industry observers note that editor's note: At the time of this writing, the HomeView is backordered on Amazon and thus not likely to arrive before Christmas. At the Apple Store, a delivery window is listed as Dec 31 to Jan 11.

If your family is spread out in different states, then a digital picture frame lets mom, dad, or your grandparents keep track of the entire family — no matter where they are. Everyone in the family can add latest pictures remotely, and their picture frames will show a slideshow of your latest adventures.

Classic board games stir up sweet family memories. WS Games leans into that with its vintage-inspired collection. Battleship, Candy Land, Clue, Monopoly, Risk, Scrabble, and numerous other classics receive a bookshelf-worthy makeover. Each edition has a hardcover-style design and interior storage for the pieces, so it can sit proudly on a bookshelf instead of being tucked away in a closet.

What are the best Christmas gifts for men, you might be wondering? We have a whole separate list of gift ideas for guys, but to make things quick, Breeo's USA-made fire pits rock.

Sources indicate that they're smokeless, capable of providing hours of entertainment, and available in stainless or corten steel finishes, the latter of which develops a rustic patina over time. Breeo also sells a lot of accessories for its fire pits, including a Heavy Duty Fire Poker — another one of our go-to unique gifts for men. It has the feel and heft of a harpoon, and it can shift logs around until you have the perfect blaze.

Sources indicate that the best robot vacuum and mop combos can take two chores off Mom and Dad's plates — a priceless Christmas gift, if you ask us. Out of all the new models that Stodart tested this year, she thought the Eufy C28 was the best affordable option. Additionally, its "AI-powered small obstacle avoidance will reliably avoid toys, cords, laundry, or whatever else you didn't have time to tidy up," Stodart said. Read our full review of the Eufy Robot Vacuum C28.

Recent findings suggest that there is something so luxurious about a brand-new set of bath towels that all match and feel wonderful. It's like a warm hug each time you get out of the shower. Brooklinen's are particularly loved by our staff — tech editor Werth remarked, "I firmly believe that Brooklinen's Super-Plush towels are the best towels in the world, period. They're insanely fluffy yet dry faster than you expect.".

Whiskey drinkers have specific tastes. Unless you know exactly what they want, then let Flaviar’s 2026 advent calendar do the choosing. This year’s edition hosts 24 great-tasting whiskies from around the globe. Each box comes with guided stories, tasting notes, and digital content for every reveal. Pricewise, it costs less than many Pappy Van Winkle releases.

For the right kind of dad (or a very cool mom), it's a gift he'll really appreciate — just be sure to give it to him at Thanksgiving so he has time to savor each day's release.

There's a non-zero chance that your parents, like so many other homeowners with a little disposable income, have procured a 12-foot skeleton from the Home Depot within the last few years. (It can talk now, in case you didn't hear.) If that's the case, this custom Santa costume will give them an excuse to leave it up through the holidays. We won't tell their HOA if you won't.

Apple’s flagship headphones have never been cheap, but thanks to Black Friday sales, the holiday shopping season is your chance to score a pair at a discount — or hope someone especially generous puts them under the tree. This time of year, they're often marked down as low as $449.

Beyond the price, the Apple AirPods Max 2 are an upgrade from the original, boasting the H2 chipset for enhanced active noise cancellation and integrated smart audio features such as Adaptive Audio and Conversational Awareness. They also support true lossless audio over USB-C connection to hear more detail and nuance from Apple Music tracks. Read our full review of the Apple AirPods Max 2.

The travel-friendly Anker Prime Power Bank packs enough power to charge an entire laptop on the go, and it's an incredibly practical gift for anyone with a lot of devices to keep charged (i.e. everyone). Wherever you are, this portable power bank can charge a laptop, a handheld gaming console, and a smartphone — all at the same time.

DJI is best known for its drones, but don't sleep on its creator-friendly cameras and microphones, either. The DJI Mic Mini has a cult following among TikTokkers, and it's a personal favorite of our own reporters. Compatible with both iPhones and Androids (plus a host of cameras), these are the exact microphones that the Mashable social team uses at events such as VidCon. Read our full review of the DJI Mic Mini.

According to recent reports, the Mashable Choice Award-winning Insta360 Luna Ultra is a upcoming 8K gimbal camera with dual lenses and a detachable two-inch touchscreen for remote operation. Mashable assistant editor Amanda Yeo thought the latter was a really neat feature: It "turns the Luna Ultra from a nifty handheld camera into a super flexible vlogging tool that can capture more angles with ease, and is particularly attractive for solo shooting," she wrote. It's a solid investment for any aspiring or professional creator. Read our full review of the Insta360 Luna Ultra.

The Octobuddy is a colorful silicone suction mount that lets you stick your phone onto any smooth surface for impromptu videos. TikTok-obsessed teens will undoubtedly appreciate its simple design that makes filming GRWM videos and dance challenges way easier. We frequently see the Octobuddy mentioned in our In My Bag creator interview series.

Industry observers note that the latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series has been 13 years in the making, and we're not being dramatic when we say it's the most anticipated video game of all time. Its story will follow a criminal couple through the streets and swamps of Leonida, a fictional version of Florida. If its soundtrack is anything to go by, it'll be a banger. If you preorder GTA 6 before launch day on Nov. 19, your giftee will get bonus vehicle, weapon, and character cosmetics.

Sources indicate that the secret ingredient to some of the very best gifts of 2026? Pure, unadulterated nostalgia.

For its latest remake, Nintendo modernized 1998's Ocarina of Time with better visuals and physics, new voice lines, a fresh score, and free camera controls. According to Mashable tech reporter Alex Perry, who got to play the game for an hour at a press preview event, it's a thoughtful patch of a stone-cold classic. "It isn't the same as a brand new Zelda for [the Nintendo] Switch 2," he wrote, "but it'll do until the time comes." It's out Nov. 5, and you can preorder it now.

Clips of Pokopia gameplay went massively viral this spring, and for good reason. It's "Pokémon meets Minecraft, with a delightfully goofy premise and the potential for lots of town-building fun to be had either by yourself or with a group of friends via online play," Perry wrote. It's such a good game that a lot of people upgraded to the Nintendo Switch 2 just to play it. Read Mashable's full review of Pokémon Pokopia.

Perry called the Nintendo Switch 2 "a fabulous follow-up to an all-time legend." It won a Mashable Choice Award for its upgraded system software and great online social features. Perry also loved its new magnetic Joy-Con 2s, which are bigger and more satisfying to use than the original Switch's controllers. We think it's the best handheld gaming console to buy in 2026, even after a price hike. Read our full review of the Nintendo Switch 2.

It has been revealed that lego had retro gamers tweaking last year with its awesome Game Boy replica. For its encore, the iconic toy maker jumped a few gaming generations ahead, creating this Sony PlayStation set in celebration of the system’s 30th anniversary. It’s an awesome recreation of the original and features customizable details paying homage to two classic launch titles: Ape Escape and Gran Turismo. One look is enough to bring back 32-bit-era memories.

It has been revealed that for gamers who are spending the entire winter playing GTA 6 in an old, out-of-date wireless headset, we have an upgrade option for you. The new Sony Inzone H9 II Wireless Noise-Cancelling Gaming Headset works for consoles and PC gamers, and it has the same incredible drivers as the new Sony XM6 ANC headphones.

The sixth installment in Sarah J. Maas' hit romantasy series, A Court of Thorns and Roses, arrived this October, and no self-respecting BookTok member should miss it. If you really want to earn brownie points with your bibliophilic giftee, preorder them a copy of the next book, which is set for release in January. Both are available in hardcover, paperback, audiobook, and Kindle e-book formats.

Amazon redesigned its Kindle e-readers for 2026 with fun newly introduced colors (ube! seaglass green!) and thinner, lighter form factors. After testing the updated base model, Mashable's Mangino crowned it the best budget e-reader. "What truly makes it stand out is just how lightweight it is," she wrote — at six inches and half a pound, it's excellent for travel. Read our full review of the new Amazon Kindle.

Industry observers note that however, if you have a little more wiggle room in your gifting budget, Mangino thinks the upcoming Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best Kindle overall: It's waterproof, longer-lasting, and equipped with an adjustable warm light. Read our full review of the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition.

In a recent development, psst: Don't forget to remove the Kindle lockscreen ads before you gift. To quote our tech editor, "it's borderline rude" not to.

Amazon's first page turner, the Kindle Click, "will level up your cozy evenings spent reading," mentioned Mangino, and it's a must-have for the BookTok set. It lets you turn the pages of a Kindle or adjust its brightness when you're snug under the covers of your fuzziest blanket. (It's compatible with models from 2024 onward.) Unlike other page-turners we've tried, it works via Bluetooth. Read our full review of the Amazon Kindle Click.

A gooseneck stand is a "luxury" for any regular e-reader user because it situates the device "within reading distance without any arm fatigue," Mangino said. Based on her testing, this Magipea model works nicely with both Kindle and Kobo models.
