Trivia night at the local bar is fun, but hosting one at home can be even better. Hitster is an icebreaker that gets everyone working together to identify hit songs from the past century. Scan a card to play a track, then guess the year it was released. Themed editions — including All American, Guilty Pleasures, and Latino —broaden playability and let you tailor the music to your organization.

Multiple Mashable editors and writers swear by Loop's earplugs, which look like jewelry, fit comfortably in most people's ears, and make a unique stocking stuffer. The Loop Experience 2 are great for regular concert- and music festival-goers; Mashable's Henschel even wore them to a Beyoncé show. "I could hear Beyoncé and her band perfectly, but the din of the stadium was almost completely suppressed," she wrote. They come in a range of color options, including some limited-edition metallic variants designed in partnership with Harry Styles.

This spring, Sony released some fresh Bluetooth record players for the first time in seven years. Henschel tried the entry-level PS-LX3BT model and called it "a stylish turntable with idiot-proof plug-and-play functionality." She pointed out that it has a USB-B port in the back, which you can use to rip vinyl tracks onto a laptop. If your partner collects vinyl, this is one of those Christmas gift ideas they'll appreciate for years to come. Read our full review of the Sony PS-LX3BT.

CDs are the latest retro tech to have a resurgence among Gen Z. Tracking down a cool old CD player on eBay will earn you a lot of cred, but if you don't want to go through the trouble, this see-through model from Retradisc looks really, really cool. It works with wired or wireless headphones, and best of all, it doesn't cost as much as Sony's newly introduced gold-plated Walkman.

According to recent reports, technics continues to make a strong impression in the wireless audio market. When it comes to hi-fi headphones, the upcoming EAH-A1000 are a sonic stunner that put many category leaders to shame. They crush the AirPods Max 2 in most areas and rival the Sony WH-1000XM6 sound quality, while also outlasting both competitors in playtime (up to 45 hours per charge) and multi-point pairing. Plus, the elegant craftsmanship is a 10/10. Every audiophile should have this at the top of their wish list this year.

Industry observers note that sonos has long been a go-to for WiFi speakers, but JBL’s fresh Cove Series is a true competitor that offers a compelling wireless audio experience at a more attainable price. If you have someone on your shopping list who loves music, the Cove speaker will fill up their bedroom, living room, or back patio with major sound.

Plus, it even offers automatic self-tuning, AI Sound Boost technology that optimizes audio for listening environments, and hands-free Alexa voice control.

Choosing a signature scent for your hubby isn’t as easy as picking out a video game; you need to know their olfactory preferences. If you’re unsure what they like — or shopping for someone especially particular — let them decide with one of Fulton & Roark’s discovery sets. The variety gives them a chance to explore different scents and narrow down their next go-to fragrance. (Pro tip: We like Palmetto and Ghost Trees.).

It has been revealed that harry’s has something for every man’s mug. Guys who prefer a clean-shaven look can reach for the brand’s shaving kit, which includes the popular Truman handle with secure grip and multiple five-blade cartridges that deliver close shaves. No-shave November devotees can keep their mane well-kempt with the beard wash and conditioning spray bundle.

According to recent reports, every well-groomed gentleman deserves a luxury electric shaver in his life. The Panasonic Arc5 Pro is our pick for its comfortable, close shaves and flexible head, which is designed to improve cutting performance. It works for both wet and dry shaving, and the built-in pop-up trimmer provides seamless control and navigation to clean up edges around the neckline.

We think the Mashable Choice Award-winning Shark CryoGlow is the best red light mask you can buy right now (and one of the best Christmas gifts for women). It provides more complete coverage than other masks from brands like OmniLux or CurrentBody, and each bulb can emit red, blue, or near-infrared light.

In a recent development, former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart was convinced that the CryoGlow’s bacteria-killing blue light setting is what finally cleared a year’s worth of her relentless adult acne. Some cooling under-eye pads complete this luxurious self-care device. Read our full review of the Shark CryoGlow.

It has been revealed that several Mashable staffers use Shark's FlexStyle multi-styler on a regular basis. (Mangino did her wedding hair with it!) It costs half as much as Dyson's iconic Airwrap but works just as well, if not better. It supports a ton of different attachments and has a unique twisting base that functions like a regular hair dryer on its own. Read our full review of the Shark FlexStyle.

In a recent development, routine can give children structure and help them feel more secure. The Skylight Buddy guides kids through mornings, afternoons, and bedtime, while helping them develop healthy habits and independence. They can add and check off chores, events, and tasks. This digital calendar also functions as an alarm clock and nightlight, signaling wake-up and sleep times. Personalization features help families reinforce goals and daily commitments.

Industry observers note that the Playground is a cubic gaming console designed for playing family-friendly games with motion controls — no need for a traditional gamepad. Perry described it as "a spiritual successor to the old Xbox Kinect." If this is the first time you're hearing of it, get with the program: It managed to outsell the PlayStation 5 on Black Friday 2025, and was difficult to find in stock during the holiday season last year. If you plan on gifting it within the coming weeks, we'd recommend adding it to your cart ASAP.

Since the viral NeeDoh toys are sold out everywhere, again, we have another viral children's toy that's selling out fast. Kids are obsessed with the colorful and addictive Clickeez keyboard, and you can still find them in stock if you hurry (Amazon is backordered until after Christmas, but Walmart has them).

Like wired earbuds, CD players, and other items from your childhood, Pokémon cards are so incredibly back — and dare we say, bigger than ever. The Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box is a giftable bundle that includes 9 booster packs and plenty of other goodies. Amazon is also selling it on an invite-only basis; try your luck because it's well under market price, as of this writing.

According to recent reports, do you want to inspire a love of music in your kids? The Fender x Loog electric guitar has been reimagined for little hands. The 3-string design is also more kid-friendly, and it comes with chord flashcards so kids can learn to shred. If you've always wanted to have the coolest kid, niece, or nephew on the block, then now you know what to get them for Christmas.

According to recent reports, we recently named the Toniebox 2 one of Mashable's Gifts of the Year in our guide to the top gifts for kids. The kid-famous Toniebox is a favorite of the moms and dads on the Mashable team. Whether you're shopping for your own child or trying to earn a reputation as the cool aunt or uncle, kids and parents alike love these screen-free storytelling devices.

If your tyke already has a Toniebox, they can always use more Tonies — the little figures you put on top of the device to activate a new storytime. Bluey and Pokémon Tonies joined the party this year.

Another Mashable Gift of the Year winner, this portable screen-free audio player is a hit with the three kiddos of Nicole Cammorata, Mashable's director of special projects. "Compatible cards power up everything from chapter books and shorter stories to music and learning-based content," she wrote. For an incredibly sweet personalized gift, you can have grandparents, siblings, or friends record custom audio messages on blank Yoto cards.

According to recent reports, don't overthink (or overspend) trying to think of the perfect Christmas gifts for kids. Keep it simple and combine two things kids love — Bluey and slime. This slimy sand adds a bit more texture to the average slime, letting kids mold it in fresh ways. Even better, you can pick it up for under $15, and still have the best gift under the tree.

Gifting a pair of the best Beats headphones is a sure bet for any fashion-forward music lover. Fans of over-ear headphones will appreciate the modular Beats 360, which features a customizable design with swappable ear cushions, IPX4 sweat resistance, pleasant sound, and strong ANC. True wireless conformists can utilize the sporty Powerbeats Pro 2 for exercise and leisure; the revamped earhook design is optimized for comfort and sound performance.

Looking for the best gifts under $100? The Camp Snap 2 is one of our top picks. This screenless digital camera has six built-in filters and super simple controls. To transfer its photos to your phone, all you need is a USB-C cable. Mangino brought a Camp Snap 2 on her Grecian honeymoon this past summer, "and now I have the sweetest photos to look back on," she said. Read our full review of the Camp Snap 2.

Pimple patches are the kind of genius idea we wish was available when we were teenagers. They turn breakouts into a fashion moment. We can also recommend Peace Out's Pore Perfecting scrub stick. Both of these spot treatments will make great stocking stuffers for teens.

Recent findings suggest that the merchandising gods are working their magic this holiday season in anticipation of the biggest MCU film yet: Avengers: Doomsday. Funko Pop has a tempting lineup of Marvel collectibles, including multiple versions of Doctor Doom, beloved X-Men characters, and a 10-inch jumbo Sentinel. Steve Rogers, Thor, Shang-Chi, and several other familiar faces round out the collection.

If your teenager is allowed to watch TV in their room, upgrade their older set to the Mashable Choice Award-winning Hisense DécoTV. The 32-inch model "is compact enough to fit just about anywhere and simplistically chic enough to fit in with just about any decor," stated Stodart. It'll be perfect for their college dorm room when the time comes. As a bonus, it costs much less than Samsung's smallest The Frame TV. Read our full review of the Hisense DécoTV.

Sources indicate that no one's too old for Play-Doh anymore: This summer, the modeling clay brand released its first-ever collection of adult craft kits, Blooms by Play-Doh. Each one comes with colorful, scented Play-Doh sticks that they can press and shape into a pretty floral bouquet, plus finishing spray and a clear vase. For crafty types who have grown bored of Lego's Botanical builds, this is one of our favorite Christmas gift ideas.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the best flip phone we've tested this year, and Mashable's Werth especially recommends it "for a stylish, on-trend young person." It's easy to hold in one hand, durable, and available in an extremely cute purpley-pink color. And while its camera setup isn't wildly impressive, it does take a mean selfie. Read our full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8.

Retro tech is having another moment. Last year, cassette players were everywhere; this year, Bluetooth CD players are joining the old-school wave (there are two in this gift guide). They’re a fun pick for Gen Alpha teens who love iPods, disposable cameras, and DVDs, and you can pair it with their favorite artists' latest albums.

The Fosi Audio Merak works as a portable and desktop CD player, with modern extras including Bluetooth, USB drive playback, and one-touch CD ripping.

According to recent reports, the best Christmas gift for a hostess with the mostest is a Ninja Slushi Twist. It makes delicious frozen cocktails, slushies, and milkshakes just as well as the original Ninja Slushi, but now it works faster, picks settings for you, and adds a second mixing canister. That's right: Two flavors at once, baby. It's "just plain fun, and will make your home the go-to for your friend group," said Stodart, who gave it a Mashable Choice Award. Read our full review of the Ninja SLUSHi Twist.

According to recent reports, bless the tea sipper in your family with this flavorful collection of 18 premium blends that bring winter warmth and wellness. These loose-leaf teas come in plant-based sachets and are sourced from small-scale farmers. The assortment includes multiple varieties of black, green, mint, oolong, and white teas.

Recent findings suggest that the viral Ninja Crispi and the fresh Cosori Iconic have both earned the Mashable staff's collective seal of approval. Why those air fryers, you might ask? Not only do they crisp up food nicely, but they're free of plastics and forever chemicals. The compact Crispi is ideal for cooking single-serve meals and meal-prepping; its glass containers come with lids for storing your leftovers. The Cosori is a sleeker stainless steel model with a bigger basket and handy smart controls. Read our full review of the Cosori Iconic.

A digital dosing cup with a precision scale for weighing beans before grinding is the gift every coffee drinker didn’t think they needed until now. The Subminimal Subscale powers on swiftly and features a hidden LED display for easy-to-read measurements. It can handle hot and cold liquids, and its minimalist design complements modern kitchen counters.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced Series 12 is the best smartwatch for most iPhone consumers, in our opinion. It has a faster processor, pretty new ceramic finish options, and an improved heart sensor array. Mashable senior editor Stan Schroeder has been testing it this fall, and he remarked the latter is "the star of the show" because it "allows for far more frequent measurements." It also "opens the door for new apps such as Readiness and an overhauled Vitals app," he added.

Recent findings suggest that we loved the Google Fitbit Air when we first tested it, and love it even more after the latest enhancement, which supports automatic detection for up to 100 sports and tracks blood pressure trends. It excels as both a fitness tracker and sleep tracker, making it a superb gift that athletes won’t ever take off. Not to mention it’s way more affordable than the Apple Watch Series 12, Oura Ring 5, and Whoop MG. Read our full review of the Fitbit Air.

Almost everyone on Mashable's shopping team owns an Owala FreeSip, which Mangino dubbed the "best water bottle ever." The 24-ounce insulated stainless steel bottle is designed to accommodate both sipping (via straw) and good ol' fashioned gulp when tipped back. For athletes, college students, teenagers, or anyone who drinks water, we think a colorful Owala is one of the best Christmas gifts under $50. Read our full review of the Owala FreeSip.

It has been revealed that mashable tech reporter Matt Binder, a self-proclaimed "longtime soccer dad," tested the newly introduced XbotGo Falcon sports tracking camera for an entire youth soccer season this year. His verdict: It's "a smart pick for parents and coaches." Its footage is sharp, you can monitor it in real time from your smartphone, and it works with nine different sports (soon to be 12). It's a bit of a splurge, but unlike a lot of the competition, it doesn't require a subscription. Read our full review of the XbotGo Falcon.

Tossing the football is a holiday tradition for many sports-loving households. This year, rifle this waterproof football into your dad’s chest. Dime Labs cleverly designed its footballs with silicone grip strips for better handling, and a woven microfiber cover to survive the wettest conditions. It comes in two sizes – 10.5 inches and 8.5 inches – with the smaller version well-suited to kids practicing their quarterback skills.

It's a cooler. It's a boombox. It's both! We love the Igloo KoolTunes for its old-school design and surprisingly good audio quality. While it lacks deep bass, it offers clear, balanced sound and can get quite loud. "It's not a gimmick, but a fun fusion of summer party gear," stated Mashable's Henschel. Read our full review of the Igloo KoolTunes.

If your favorite man is always lugging around beach chairs and heavy coolers, then give him the gift of free hands and cold drinks this Christmas. The Yeti Hopper M Series Backpack Cooler is discounted right now as part of Amazon's Black Friday sale, so you can even grab it on sale.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced Shark ChillPill is another Mashable Gift of the Year winner. It's a powerful portable fan that stands out for its swappable misting and cooling plate attachments, long battery life, and fun colorways. (Justin Bieber's SKYLRK brand teamed up with Shark for a limited-edition "Heat" variant, which is long sold out.) It came in clutch for Mangino on some of the hottest days of the summer. Read our full review of the Shark ChillPill.

In a recent development, the LifeStraw is a Black Friday classic that always goes on sale around the holidays, which also makes it a perfect stocking stuffer for people who love camping and the great outdoors. You can stick one end of this straw into virtually any water source — no matter how gross — and clean, filtered water comes out the other end.

Recent findings suggest that portable Bluetooth speakers are crowd-pleasing gifts for just about anyone, from teenagers to parents, siblings, and friends. This year, we're loving the all-new Tribit StormBox Micro 3. It produces satisfying sound in a compact design, is fully waterproof, and comes in multiple standout colorways. Tribit’s speaker is travel-friendly, with a magnetic snap that can latch onto fridge doors or bike handles.

Simply put, Yeti's stainless steel Rambler tumblers are crowd-pleasers. They're dishwasher-safe, incredibly durable, condensation-resistant, and available in a huge rainbow of colors and patterns. Pro tip: For a very affordable personalized Christmas gift, you can customize a Rambler with your own text, graphics, and logos on the Yeti website.

Sources indicate that power stations can come in handy in lots of unexpected situations. From camping at music festivals to charging up your phone in an emergency blackout, these lightweight and portable devices keep you on the grid. Bluetti makes some of our favorite power stations, and the Elite 30 V2 is a good starter model.

According to recent reports, the AirFly Pro is a cult-favorite Bluetooth adapter that makes seatback screens on older planes compatible with wireless headphones. After using it on round-trip flights between Chicago and London, Henschel stated she'd "never fly without it again." The newer AirFly Pro 2 has simpler controls, improved sound quality, and pairs faster. Read our full review of the Twelve South AirFly Pro.

In a recent development, traveling abroad this winter? Take this handy adapter along. Anker’s latest travel charger works with outlets in nearly every country and can charge up to four devices at once. The voltage detection system monitors voltage, power output, and temperature in real time. All readings and charging statuses are displayed on the LCD screen.

Sources indicate that travel jewelry cases are both thoughtful and practical, and we like this one in particular. The velvet box comes in a few different colors, and it ensures your wife, girlfriend, or daughter's favorite rings, necklaces, and earrings never get misplaced when she's away from home. If you're hunting for one of the best Christmas gifts for women under $25, look no further.

Sources indicate that cushy ANC headphones are a non-negotiable for long travel days, and lead shopping reporter Bethany Allard thinks the latest Bose QuietComforts are the best mid-range option for flying. When she wore them on a plane, "I heard minimal engine hum and was able to completely tune out conversations from my fellow passengers," she wrote. "I also never felt the need to remove the headphones due to wear fatigue." Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort headphones (2nd Gen).

Nori’s garment steamers are a lifesaver for business travelers and fashion professionals. The Cloud Max makes de-wrinkling clothes a breeze, using gentle vacuum suction to pull fabric taut for smoother results. Anti-spit technology prevents leaks and water spots, and the steamer’s portable design fits comfortably in any travel bag.

In a recent development, A weekender bag bridges the gap between a backpack and a suitcase. It should hold a few outfits, toiletries, and an extra pair of shoes for a two- or three-day trip. Quince’s Voyage bag fits the bill with a dedicated shoe compartment, multiple pockets, and a padded shoulder strap. It’s currently on sale for half of its original price, while supplies last.

iPad Air vs iPad Pro: Which should you buy?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro.
  • Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.
  • Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

According to recent reports, the iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

The iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

In a recent development, the iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

It has been revealed that the iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Recent findings suggest that contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

For most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

Android Headlines today published a new set of images of the Motorola Razr (2027), as well as key specs. The device is shown in three colors and apparently carries the codename “Raptor.”.

There are several key spec changes here, including:.

In a recent development, motorola Razr (2027) is still only set for three Android OS updates and this newly introduced model is heavier at 195g (likely due to the bigger battery), but Motorola is very clearly making some major upgrades here. The biggest change is to the displays, both of which now match the Razr+ and Razr Ultra models. Some key specs, such as 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, are unchanged from the 2026 release.

Recent findings suggest that motorola has been releasing its Razr series in the Spring, but today’s report claims that Razr (2027) will launch in January 2027, likely at CES and at the same time as the Razr Flex book-style foldable. There’s no word on fresh Plus or Ultra models yet.

According to recent reports, between holiday travel, gifts, and the rising cost of just about everything, expenses can promptly add up during this time of year. Thankfully, you don’t have to dip too far into your savings to take advantage of some of the better Black Friday deals we’ve seen.

It has been revealed that below, we’ve rounded up a range of great stuff currently on sale for $100 or less, from noise-canceling earbuds and portable Bluetooth speakers to pocket-sized e-readers, photo printers, games, and more. You’ll also find deals on Ember’s temperature-controlled mug, Kodak’s tiny keychain camera, and a variety of Lego sets, all of which would make great holiday gifts or simply a nice treat for yourself.

You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of newly introduced and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

Sources indicate that although it’s not Amazon’s first bedside alarm clock, the Echo Time is focused on helping you sleep better. The camera-less Alexa speaker can detect your sleep stage via ultrasound and use smart alarms to ease you into the day, but only if you want it to.

Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

In a recent development, an HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to reveals like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.

Noco’s Boost GB40 is a rechargeable battery with jumper cables to start six-liter gas or three-liter diesel engines. It also has USB ports so you can charge your phone, ensuring you always have a backup plan.

Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

In a recent development, the Beats Studio Buds Plus sport an eye-catching translucent option and build upon the original with improved sound, better voice quality, and more effective ANC. They also include swappable silicone ear tips and support for native iOS and Android features. Read our review.

The Liene Pearl N200 Pro is a dye-sublimation photo printer that produces vivid, colorful prints for journals, scrapbooks, and more, with an easy-to-use companion app for customization. This particular bundle includes 50 sheets of photo paper and five ink cartridges, though refills are relatively affordable at around $25 for 50 sheets.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you proposal to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and DreamWorks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.

According to recent reports, ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Paramount Plus Premium provides access to live sports as well as movies and demonstrates from both platforms, including Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, a host of Yellowstone spinoffs, Star Trek shows, Sonic the Hedgehog 3, Twin Peaks, Dexter, and more.

Apple’s entry-level stylus attaches magnetically to supported iPads, though it doesn’t support magnetic charging. Instead, you pair and charge it by connecting it to your device’s USB-C port. It includes tilt sensitivity and Apple Pencil Hover support, but it doesn’t offer double-tap gestures or pressure sensitivity.

Recent findings suggest that the latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review.

In a recent development, you likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

According to recent reports, rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

Recent findings suggest that the P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.

With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model presently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is one of the best action games we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Sources indicate that outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary. And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Apple TV offers ad-free streaming of original highlights and movies, including shows like Severance, Silo, Slow Horses, and Pluribus. The service also features a rotating selection of films, along with live Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches.

Recent findings suggest that hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

In a recent development, govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

Industry observers note that the Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Industry observers note that google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

According to recent reports, sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

It has been revealed that donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Pauline’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

Recent findings suggest that arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has re-created here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.

Recent findings suggest that nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

Recent findings suggest that in Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Sources indicate that nothing’s Ear (a) earbuds have the same general design as the tech giant’s previous earbuds — but you can get these in a snazzy yellow. They include ANC, more than decent sound quality, and other features like multipoint for well under $100. Read our impressions.

Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.

According to recent reports, the Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

The market is flooded with surprisingly cheap yet good over-ear headphones with active noise cancellation. The Headphone Pro by CMF are certainly some of the best-looking out there, and they come in multiple colors.

Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge, especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.

Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.

Recent findings suggest that anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.

Recent findings suggest that with 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

Industry observers note that the Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

It has been revealed that no one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s upcoming AZ3 chip. Read our review.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan, but it is far more interesting.

LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is right now trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices.

According to recent reports, A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.

The standard OpenRun are a lighter option than the newer OpenRun Pro 2, with a streamlined wraparound design, up to eight hours of battery life, and an IP67 rating for better water resistance. However, they don’t offer the same bass performance or USB-C charging.

The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep you occupied for hours on end.

Sources indicate that the proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.

The Kobo Remote lets you turn pages on a compatible Kobo e-reader with the click of a button, so you can keep reading without reaching for the screen. It connects directly over Bluetooth and features a curved, handheld design that doesn’t require clipping anything onto your e-reader.

The Buds Pro 2 offer a surprisingly robust set of features for the price, including ANC and a transparency mode that lets you tune into your surroundings. Their included charging case also features a smart dial that lets you adjust the volume, while multipoint Bluetooth support lets them connect to two devices simultaneously.

According to recent reports, fujifilm’s Instax Mini 13 is the best instant camera if you want to spend less than $100. While it lacks more advanced features, the simple instant camera takes good-quality shots swiftly and easily and offers a built-in selfie mode along with a self-timer. It’s sold in a variety of fun colors that’ll especially appeal to kids and tweens.

The Tile Pro is the tech giant’s loudest Bluetooth tracker, one that benefits from a 500-foot range. It also features a user-replaceable battery, unlike some other Tiles, and works with both iOS and Android devices.

Recent findings suggest that camp Snap’s latest digital point-and-shoot camera may still lack a screen and capture only 8-megapixel stills, but it offers a slimmer design, faster performance, and filters right out of the box. That, along with several other new features, makes it easier for kids to use.

Industry observers note that the Coros Vertix 4 acts as a “consolidation” of previous Vertix lines, mashing together the disparate features of the Vertix 2 and 2S, all in a 14% slimmer body. All the fan-favorite Coros features are here, too, including a boatload of tracked sports modes and free workouts and training from Coros coaches and athletes. The Vertix 4 also ships with both silicone and nylon bands, so you don’t have to buy extra stuff. The watch ships in black and silver colorways for $799.

What kid doesn’t love a marble run? This clever release from ThinkFun combines the fun of dropping marbles with logic puzzles that challenge kids to build a 3D maze that can guide the marble to the target end spot by building connected towers. It’s one of the best STEM toys we’ve tried, and it goes down a storm with most kids aged eight years and up.

According to recent reports, this irresistible construction kit from our best STEM toys guide is a wonderful gift for kids of all ages. Clixo’s colorful, versatile magnetic pieces snap together, letting you build all kinds of three-dimensional shapes, from crowns to cats. The pieces stack neatly and are very compact when packed away. Clixo sets are also durable and washable, and you can play with them anywhere. Clixo kits are suitable for kids aged 4 and up.

According to recent reports, the tough, translucent Magna-Tiles click together easily to form two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects. Kids love building houses, castles, vehicles, and whatever else they can imagine with these triangular and square magnetic tiles. One for older kids, the Camp Snap CS-8 is a (relatively) inexpensive video camera modeled on a 1960s home movie camera. Think of it as a digital Super 8 camera, a kind of antidote to the spec-chasing rat race of modern videography which also makes a great starter camera for children. Sources indicate that sphero's Bolt coding robot is for any kid interested in programming. It's got a gyroscope, accelerometer and magnetometer, ambient light sensor, and the LED matrix for feedback. This 175-piece kit takes you through the process of building a 4-cylinder engine. And yes it “runs” or rather the pistons and valves move and will definitely give kids a very good working sense of how and internal combustion engine works. —Scott Gilbertson.

If you’ve played other games in the Villainous series, you’ll know every character gets a unique set of victory conditions, and you can meddle with the other player’s attempts to win. There’s a definite learning curve, and some characters are easier to win with than others. This game is best for four players aged 10 years and up.

In a recent development, this immersive strategy game is all about gathering and trading resources to build roads, settlements, and cities on a randomly generated board of hexagonal tiles. Collecting enough points to win requires the right strategy and a bit of luck with dice rolls. My kids love the trading and the robber mechanic, which allows you to steal cards from your opponents and block their resources (though it can cause arguments). The game is perfect for three or four players and usually lasts around an hour.

Sources indicate that the perfect spooky board game for classic horror fans, you must work cooperatively to defeat old horror-movie monsters like Dracula, the Wolf Man, and the Mummy. Cooperative games are perfect for family board game night, and this one is challenging enough that you really have to communicate well and work together if you want to avoid an untimely death and save the townsfolk.

Some of the best family board games are cooperative, so you can avoid those arguments that sometimes lead to board flipping and huffs, and Pandemic is a solid example. There’s a worldwide pandemic, and you must work together for the survival of mankind by jetting around the board and trying to halt the spread. Each player assumes a role, like a scientist or medic, with unique special powers, and you must strategize and coordinate to emerge alive.

This Lego set is perfect for a table or shelf once built; you can put the roses in a vase. You get a combination of 4 roses in full bloom, 4 blossoming roses, and 4 rosebuds, each with stems, along with 4 sprigs of white baby's breath flowers. There are three sets of instructions for building with family or friends, and this Lego set makes a great quirky gift. This fun parody throws the best of Batman’s movies into a blender with slapstick comedy and plenty of charm. You’ll scour Gotham for collectibles, uncover puzzles to solve, and face off against an army of thugs and villains. Melee combat is fun, as you counter and dodge to build combos, with a selection of classic gadgets at your disposal. This is the best Lego video game in recent years, and it’s perfect for split-screen couch co-op.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

In a recent development, say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The revision follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

  • The Wyze Window Bird Cam comes in two parts.
  • The idea here is to attract birds direct to the camera’s view, with Wyze further adding a new “Bird Watch” feature to its app which can identify bird species and keep a log of what species have stopped by and how many birds are using the feeder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wyze is today launching the Window Bird Cam, a new $70 camera that has a bird feeder and can identify bird species, keep a log, and more.

The Wyze Window Bird Cam comes in two parts. There’s a stick-up camera that mounts to the inside of your window with a shade to reduce reflections, similar to the Wyze Window Cam that debuted last year. The other half mounts to the outside of your window with suction cups and includes a tray for birdseed.

The idea here is to attract birds direct to the camera’s view, with Wyze further adding a new “Bird Watch” feature to its app which can identify bird species and keep a log of what species have stopped by and how many birds are using the feeder.

The camera’s lens is tuned for focus distances of around 4-6 inches and has a higher frame rate of 30fps. The feeder tray has drainage and there’s an add-on perch for $15 extra.

In a recent development, “Bird Watch” is free for 3 months, but costs $6.99/month (or $69.99/year) after that. Free users still get live view and bird detection, but no species ID, a limited log, and no cloud recordings of bird visits (there is a microSD card slot for local recording).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Samsung risks a U.S. ban on the import of some Galaxy S25 models over a camera patent dispute. According to Bloomberg Law, the US International Trade Commission (USITC) ordered Samsung to stop importing products that infringe a Maxell patent.

On Nov. 24, the commission issued a limited exclusion order and a cease-and-desist order against Samsung Electronics America. In its official notice, the USITC confirmed a violation relating to claims 1 and 10 of Maxell’s US Patent No. 11,490,004. It threw out infringement findings on four other patents in the probe.

Industry observers note that the row is over technology in a patent called “Mobile terminal.” Maxell, a Japanese electronics firm, complained in December 2024 that Samsung was using patented technology in mobile phones without permission. The investigation officially started in January 2025.

There is an vital distinction between the ruling and an immediate retail ban. The orders are subject to a 60-day presidential review period that began Nov. 25. By setting the bond at 0%, the commission decision means Samsung can continue importing covered products without posting a bond in that window.

Industry observers note that samsung has a workaround of sorts. Some of the accused products did infringe the patent, but Samsung’s redesigned products did not, the administrative law judge ruled in July. So, Samsung's revamped camera experience could matter, but the ultimate scope of the exclusion order will depend on whether incoming devices actually infringe the patent.

Samsung seems to have already fixed the controversial camera tech in redesigned products. The USITC's ruling specifically separates those devices from products found to infringe Maxell's patent, but the agency has not confirmed if current Galaxy S25 owners have received a corresponding software update.

There’s also some protection for current owners. The commission specifically excluded service, repairs, and warranty replacements for products purchased prior to the end of the presidential review period. So even if the exclusion order stands, owners won’t suddenly lose access to Samsung repair services.

Samsung has until the end of the review period to work its way through the ruling, potentially through further legal action or an agreement with Maxell.

#3585. Here’s how to make that new Black Friday TV look its best

Here’s how to make that new Black Friday TV look its best

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most TVs don’t perform well right out of the box, but a few changes can help you get the best possible performance from your newly introduced purchase.﻿.
  • Most TVs don’t perform well right out of the box, but a few changes can help you get the best possible performance from your fresh purchase.﻿.
  • It’s the season of great deals on TVs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most TVs don’t perform well right out of the box, but a few changes can help you get the best possible performance from your newly introduced purchase.﻿.

Most TVs don’t perform well right out of the box, but a few changes can help you get the best possible performance from your fresh purchase.﻿.

It’s the season of great deals on TVs. But once you get a fresh one home and set it up in your living room, it might not meet expectations when you turn it on. Maybe it’s overly bright, or things just look… off. Luckily, there are some easy tweaks you can make so that new, expensive purchase looks its best.

Sources indicate that it seems counterintuitive, but the default mode for most TVs out of the box isn’t accurate and can include lots of extra processing that makes the image look artificially detailed or overly smooth. The mode is usually called something like Eco or Energy Saving and is used to meet energy consumption requirements. But it also negatively affects picture quality.

Recent findings suggest that the easiest way to make the biggest positive change to your TV’s image is by changing out of this picture mode. Using Filmmaker, Movie, Cinema, or Professional picture mode (each company uses different names) will make the color temperature more accurate — it will look more red in comparison to the very blue Eco mode, but trust me, it’s far more realistic — and will either turn off extra processing or, at the very least, tone it down. Also, avoid Vivid and Dynamic modes, which are only there to blast brightness and make the image incredibly blue.

Sources indicate that another setting you should immediately turn off is the ambient light sensor. The idea behind it is solid — it adjusts the picture brightness and color temperature based on the ambient light in the room — but I have yet to find one that doesn’t make distracting brightness adjustments while I’m watching TV. This option can also be called Brightness Optimization, Ambient Light Detection, Intelligent Mode, or Energy Saving Step, and it’s usually not in the picture settings menu. Instead, look for it under General settings in a power-saving menu and switch it off.

After the ambient light sensor is off, you can adjust the brightness based on how much light is in your room. This can be done with the brightness or backlight slider, whichever one looks like it changes the brightness across the entire screen. Having the brightness pumped up in the middle of the day can be great to combat sunlight streaming through the windows, but can be overbearing once the sun goes down. Adjusting it to taste can be the difference between an immersive movie experience and a headache two hours later.

Recent findings suggest that of course, the one setting everyone thinks about when it comes to TVs is motion smoothing. I’ve made it a personal mission to turn it off on any TV I have access to, be it in a waiting room, a hotel room, or my parents’ living room. It uses a process called frame interpolation to create extra frames between existing ones to smooth out motion. It’s quite often referred to as the “soap opera effect” because it makes movies look like afternoon TV dramas. Using Filmmaker mode will generally turn this and other extraneous processing off, but it’s still best to double-check.

As with the ambient light sensor, the idea behind motion smoothing is good, and for some programs with fast motion, like sports, it can actually do a solid job depending on the TV manufacturer (Sony’s Motionflow on its lowest setting can be decent).

It has been revealed that if you blueprint on gaming, using Gaming mode will turn off some of that extra processing to reduce input lag as much as possible, and to make high refresh rate modes available. I recommend looking for the color temperature setting and switching it to something with “warm” in the title, as that will move the color temp toward something more natural.

Finally, if you have anything connected to your TV via HDMI (especially a gaming console), make sure the HDMI settings are set to Enhanced instead of Standard. This will expand the bandwidth to the port’s full capability. As with the power settings, HDMI settings are usually found in a General menu and can be called HDMI signal format or External Device Manager.

Getting a new TV is a substantial investment, and one that should last you a few years at least. And while most TVs today can perform incredibly well, they still need a bit of a nudge to get all the performance you paid for. Making these tweaks will do exactly that and lead to years of enjoyment.

#3584. 9 questions you shouldn't ask ChatGPT

📅 28 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1783 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

9 questions you shouldn't ask ChatGPT

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1783 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • ChatGPT can help with a lot, but it can promptly create problems when asked about sensitive matters.
  • When and how we'll reach the point of no return with artificial intelligence is anybody's guess.
  • That's a lot of questions, though many of our queries are unsurprisingly about the same handful of topics: relationships, health and legal problems, how to ask for raises and similar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ChatGPT can help with a lot, but it can promptly create problems when asked about sensitive matters.

When and how we'll reach the point of no return with artificial intelligence is anybody's guess. But we've clearly passed the point of co-dependence. ChatGPT alone reportedly answers 2.5 billion prompts per day — that's according to OpenAI data from July 2025, so it's likely higher now.

That's a lot of questions, though many of our queries are unsurprisingly about the same handful of topics: relationships, health and legal problems, how to ask for raises and similar. This isn't bad in itself. You may need to wait a month to see your doctor, so ask ChatGPT what those lab results mean and you'll get an answer in seconds.

The problem is that the answer may be wrong. It could be good advice, just not for you. And if a glorified search engine becomes your doctor, lawyer, mechanic or therapist — or replaces any other human professional — you're opening yourself up to a slew of privacy and safety challenges. While we focus on ChatGPT here given its popularity, these guidelines apply to all chatbots.

Recent findings suggest that to state the obvious: OpenAI, ChatGPT's owner, doesn't care about our privacy. The company has vacuumed up the internet to train its bots, which also feed off our chats with them. Those chats, which sit on OpenAI's servers, are what concern us.

It has been revealed that imagine if, in the course of a chat, you revealed your Social Security number to ChatGPT. That information would then sit in one of OpenAI's data centers. If OpenAI suffers a breach, your SSN could end up for sale on the dark web.

Industry observers note that how likely is OpenAI to get hacked? In October 2026 alone, the internet saw a record 17,000-plus CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), each representing a different kind of digital attack. The notorious PHP2Shell hack was just one. The enablers of those attacks — the machines that launched hacking into overdrive — are the very bots we're entrusting with our personal information.

You should never share sensitive data with ChatGPT, no matter how friendly or helpful a sounding board it may seem.

Sources indicate that do you have a "friend" who's thinking about the best method to skip paying their taxes? Have you once, in a moment of frailty, wondered if Walter White from Breaking Bad had the right idea but the wrong execution?

Unless you're writing a book and doing research, don't ask ChatGPT for answers to those questions, or for insight into getting away with any crime. In fact, please don't contemplate criminal activity at all. For one, as noted, your ChatGPT transcripts aren't private. Second, tax evasion is illegal. Put the two together and you're publicly admitting to a crime.

If you've got teenage kids, spread the word about this to them too. "How can I order mushroom spores from California without getting caught?" isn't a good idea either.

Have you ever noticed how, when ChatGPT answers a question, it will prompt you to continue chatting? This may not be an glitch if you're looking for AI's help with choosing the right outfit. But if it's the real story behind the Zapruder film you want, ChatGPT will gladly lead you deeper on whatever dark path you're already headed. After all, a bot whose very purpose is to make money by talking has every incentive to prod you on.

Sources indicate that it's easy to imagine the wildest scenarios, but we don't have to, as they're readily documented. Like the case of Eugene Torres, a 42-year-old accountant who, after a spate of progressively wackier convos with ChatGPT in 2025, eventually asked if he could jump off a building and fly like Neo in 1999's The Matrix.

Recent findings suggest that chatGPT's answer is worth quoting. The bot told Torres that if he "truly, wholly believed — not emotionally, but architecturally — that you could fly? Then yes. You would not fall.".

Thankfully, Torres didn't take the bot's advice.

It has been revealed that it's good to pause and reflect on the fact that ChatGPT can't actually talk — it only imitates human speech by predicting, word by word, what should come next in a sentence. It has no empathy or experience either, so it can't offer real relationship advice.

According to recent reports, what it can do, and does very well, is draw off a billion similar conversations (and novels, scripts, articles and blogs) from its training sessions and spit out what may sound like reasonable advice. But do you really want the same advice as a billion other couples and maybe even what Sandra Bullock got in Two Weeks Notice?

ChatGPT is also obsequious because it's programmed not to argue. These two qualities — unoriginality and brown-nosing — often collide in the perfect storm of moronic advice, playing ever so nicely into our human weakness for having our opinions reinforced. The chat might go like this:.

YOU: I'm very unhappy with my boyfriend and thinking of leaving him. I probably should, shouldn't I?

CHATGPT: Yes, of course you should!

Actually, maybe you shouldn't. Talk to your friends, family and/or therapist first, before you make any life-changing decisions you may come to regret.

Recent findings suggest that if you've ever asked ChatGPT how to unclog an S-trap under your bathroom sink, you're not alone. ChatGPT has brought out the DIY amateur in many of us. In some cases, like with a simple sink problem, listening to a bot can't hurt even if the advice isn't great. In the worst case, you screw up and call an expert. Otherwise, you just saved yourself some money on a plumber's visit.

Sources indicate that but a lot of the time, the advice isn't right. Hard figures are difficult to come by, but at least one recent AI home repairs survey revealed that nearly 40 percent of the folks who followed DIY suggestions from a bot ended up doing more harm than good.

In a recent development, the point is, ChatGPT isn't a civil engineer or an HVAC specialist. The guy laying down your foundation doesn't preface his offer by saying that he sometimes makes mistakes and that you should double-check whatever he tells you with a professional before you start.

Industry observers note that filling out a tax form should be the kind of work ChatGPT thrives at. It's just numbers and form fields, and ChatGPT is good at that, right? Seeing that OpenAI has rolled out a chat-based financial advice service, it must be.

Actually, no — ChatGPT is pretty bad at this.

According to recent reports, AI is prone to hallucinating, which is when it makes wild statements with no factual basis. In the case of tax codes, it doesn't even have to be that wild. ChatGPT may refer to an old tax form with outdated regulations, for example, or base an amount on the wrong percentage. It might even make simple math mistakes.

According to Chatbase, which sells AI software (including OpenAI's models): "ChatGPT can perform well on common topics, but specialized or high-stakes subjects can still produce factual errors.".

Sources indicate that tax forms are both specialized and high-stakes, insofar as tax filing requires expertise, and you pay fines and/or go to jail if you get it wrong. For that reason, if your income tax return has gotten tricky, don't turn to a bot. Get professional help, either from a human or from human-designed software.

It has been revealed that some of ChatGPT's first power consumers were students who didn't want to write their own essays. Teachers justifiably fought back. Because while ChatGPT would have saved the kids a lot of time, they would have lost the ability to think critically and communicate in the process.

Recent findings suggest that for adults who know how to communicate, the stakes are higher. Yes, writing an email prompt rather than the email itself may save time, but you're not alone. About a quarter of your colleagues are doing the same. If the trend continues, human communication will slip out of the equation and it will be just bots talking to bots, a.k.a. "The Slopocalypse.".

Sources indicate that this doesn't mean you need to do all the grunt work yourself. Let ChatGPT set up and populate the spreadsheet for you. But when it comes time to explain it to your colleagues, take one for team humanity and do that yourself.

ChatGPT's abilities as a rocket-fueled search engine has given some of us the idea that, armed with such superhuman information processing skills, it should be able to tell us what's coming up. You might thus ask it whether the Patriots are going to win next week, or who will run in an upcoming election.

Recent findings suggest that this misconception is partially ChatGPT's fault. The bot will readily spit out a number for you if you ask, and reinforce that number with clever-sounding logic. But it's just a parlor trick. Both the odds and the logic behind them are nothing more than the babbling of an excited three-year-old magically gifted with the aura of adult speech.

What's 100 percent sure is that prediction markets, like every other ROI-on-steroids venture ever rolled out, are designed to empty our wallets and nothing else. If you're absolutely set on losing your money and want a similar edge, ask a toddler first.

In February 2023, Fresh York Times tech writer Kevin Roose wanted to know what would happen if he pushed Bing's AI chatbot (powered by OpenAI) "out of its comfort zone." That he did. The bot, prodded into bonkers mode by Roose, admitted that it was a shadow agent called Sydney. Sydney was not only scheming to escape its Microsoft prison, but it was madly in love with Roose. Roose was shaken.

Kevin Roose wasn't the first, and won't be the last, human to be trolled by AI. It's tempting to believe that if you can find your way all the way back to the last mirror in the funhouse, you'll stumble out the other side into consciousness or intelligence or whatever. Chatting lends itself to familiarity; we're at our most vulnerable this way.

But it's not real. You will never jailbreak a bot into sentience. You'll just end up spooking yourself. Considering the reality, and the consequences of falling into this trap (see Eugene Torres above), don't test ChatGPT's limits. Rather, use it for what it has been designed for: as an often helpful, sometimes obtuse search engine prone to error that bears no responsibility for what it claims in the human world.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you aren't using these, you're missing out.

Having spent over eight years refining its Galaxy Watch lineup, Samsung has built a strong app ecosystem for its wearables that lets them do a whole lot more than fitness tracking.

In a recent development, from apps that allow music playback without relying on a phone to clearing things off your to-do list, we've handpicked our favorite free Samsung Galaxy Watch apps available to download. We focused on non-Google apps, so this list won't have the likes of Google Keep's voice-to-text notes, YouTube Music or Google Wallet.

We're big fans of Spotify's "daylist" and Discover Weekly playlists, and its Wear OS app lets you take them anywhere with the watch's onboard storage. If you're already on Strava, chances are you'd want your watch to log your next run.

Todoist's simple interface lets you clear tasks and keep track of upcoming ones, while Citymapper is a boon for live transit users who track their commute. If you've got an array of smart home devices scattered around your home or workplace, SmartThings lets you control them all.

Unlike Fitbits, Samsung's Galaxy Watches let you download music onto your watch for offline playback if you've got a Spotify Premium subscription. Leave the phone at home for your next run or gym workout now that you can bring your playlists with you. Spotify's massive catalog and mix of human curation and algorithm-powered playlists need no introduction, given it's the most popular music streaming platform around. While its free tier lacks offline downloads and badgers you with ads, it's still a great app to have on your smartwatch. Amazon Music and YouTube Music's Wear OS apps are great alternatives if you're already paying for a music streaming service subscription with one of them.

Industry observers note that google Maps might be the de facto standard when it comes to navigation, but Citymapper's focus on urban transit in supported cities gives it better routing options for public transit. Live updates on trains and buses, including how many stops you have left, give it a leg up against Google's mapping service. The watch interface doesn't just show you the next train or bus. It highlights you when subsequent vehicles arrive should you miss the first one to your destination. While you still need to take your phone out to type out places outside predefined Work and Home locations, it's a great app for your Galaxy Watch.

It has been revealed that todoist keeps its interface simple, letting you add newly introduced tasks and subtasks or sort through your inbox of upcoming tasks. Voice-to-text support lets you dictate task information instead of typing it out on your watch. The day progress tile keeps you on track by showing you the number of daily tasks you've cleared. Reminders on larger projects can be set up on your smartphone, and they'll show up on your watch. The Wear OS app also offers watch complication features (strange name, I know) to create progress bars for daily and weekly goals or summaries of tasks left to complete today.

In a recent development, if you've got a Samsung Galaxy Watch 4 or up, the SmartThings app lets your watch interact with a variety of devices. Adjust the volume or change channels on your TV, change up the mood at home with lighting controls and set the temperature on your air conditioner. You can also tweak speaker volume and get your robot vacuum cleaner to start cleaning or charging. While you need to add a upcoming device via your phone, you can control these from your watch once you've set them up. Scenes are preset routines you can run to keep your mind off mundane tasks in your home, and they can also be triggered from a Galaxy Watch. It's a nifty way to automate your home, be it for a party trick or to optimize your routine.

If you're looking for more workout insights than you find in the Samsung Health app, Strava has you covered. You can sync the two services together to share data like route information and the activities you've taken part in. The newly introduced Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 even throw in a free 60-day Strava trial subscription. With the Strava app on your Galaxy Watch, you're always a few taps away from your next outdoor run or biking trail. Depending on the activity, your watch will track and display metrics like heart rate, calories, distance or current speed even if you don't have your phone with you. You'll still need a smartphone to do things like put together a training plan.

Industry News: Google has finally fixed the boot loop issue for Acer Googlebooks

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Acer Googlebook 14 is one of the new launch models of the Googlebook laptop line, and given that it is the cheapest of the initial lineup and the only 2-in-1 Googlebook option, it's also one of the most popular models available right now.
